Choose the option that is the first part of this paper's abstract (every option is from a paper in Research and Theory).

criteria.A: Infection preventionists (IPs) operate in dynamic health care environments addressing evolving infectious and organizational challenges. This study investigates how career stages are associated with perceptions of leadership, support, and clinical relationships, and their impact on job satisfaction and mental health.

criteria.Z: Increasing healthcare demands and rapid technological advancements have intensified pressures on hospital organizations, highlighting the critical role of nurses’ innovative behavior in ensuring adaptive and patient-centered care.
criteria.AA: To explore how nursing and midwifery (N&M) leaders draw on professional identity to navigate their role in relation to workforce wellbeing and psychological safety, and the consequences of this work when conducted within hostile organisational cultures.
criteria.AB: The transition from nursing education to professional practice can expose new graduate nurses to transition shock and workplace stress. Structured rotation programmes may support this transition, but Kuwait-specific evidence is limited.
criteria.AC: Job satisfaction among professional nurses is a key factor that has been proven to influence the quality of healthcare, safety of patients and retention of staff at workplace.

criteria.A: Physical education (PE) is an underused setting for resistance training (Cox et al., 2020). This cluster-randomized controlled trial evaluated a combined resistance and plyometric circuit integrated into PE over 12 weeks on motor performance in lower secondary students.

questions.instructions:

Each option below is the beginning of the abstract of an article from the same subject area (Toxicology). Which option is the beginning of this article's abstract?

criteria.A: Post-marketing safety surveillance is essential for ensuring vaccine safety and maintaining public trust, particularly in African settings where evidence on the safety of COVID-19 vaccines remains limited.
criteria.B: Ifosfamide, an alkylating agent used to treat various malignancies, has limited real-world safety data on neurotoxicity. Therefore, this study analyzed ifosfamide-related Central Nervous System Adverse Events (CNS AEs) to provide a reference for drug risk management.
criteria.C: The primary objective of pharmacovigilance is the early detection and characterization of safety signals, defined as information suggesting new potential causal association between a medicinal product and an adverse event requiring further investigation.
criteria.D: This study aims to investigate the potential association between 13 disease-modifying immunosuppressive drugs used to treat multiple sclerosis and intervertebral disc herniation, thereby filling a gap in pharmacovigilance research in this field.
criteria.E: Retroperitoneal fibrosis (RPF) is a rare fibroinflammatory disorder characterized by the development of fibrotic tissue around the abdominal aorta, often leading to ureteral entrapment and renal dysfunction.
criteria.F: This study presents the development and validation of a one-step extraction method coupled with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) for the simultaneous analysis of 100 compounds in human hair.
criteria.G: Organochalcogen compounds play an essential role in redox biology, such as in the reduction of hydroperoxides by thiol‐based proteins. In vivo, this function is notably mediated by sulfur‐ and selenium‐based enzymes like glutathione peroxidases (GPxs).
criteria.H: To assess whether auditory adverse event (AE) reporting changed after the COVID-19 vaccine rollout, and whether any change reflected a true safety signal or a shift in reporting behavior.
criteria.I: Dermatology chatbots are increasingly used for patient engagement and triage, generating large volumes of patient-reported data. Objective: To examine the nature of patient-reported adverse reactions and evaluate machine learning approaches for early detection of unresolved chatbot interactions.
criteria.J: Food safety complaint systems contain large numbers of heterogeneous adverse-event reports, but surveillance use requires reproducible data sources and interpretable rules for ranking reports that may involve severe outcomes.
criteria.K: Datopotamab deruxtecan was approved in 2025 for hormone receptor-positive, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer and for EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); its safety profile in routine use has not been described.
criteria.L: Anifrolumab is a type I interferon receptor antagonist approved for adults with moderate-to-severe systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Although clinical trials established its efficacy and expected safety profile, post-marketing analyses using public EudraVigilance data remain limited.
criteria.M: Givinostat was recently approved for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), but its real-world safety profile remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated givinostat-associated safety signals by data mining of the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database.
criteria.N: Anticoagulant rodenticides (ARs) are important toxicants in veterinary forensic investigations involving suspected poisoning in cats.
criteria.O: Simultaneous identification and quantification of illicit drugs can substantially reduce the reliance on multiple analytical instruments and lower operational costs.
criteria.P: By 2021, regulatory agencies had approved two glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), semaglutide and liraglutide, for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity.
criteria.Q: Concerns regarding the psychiatric safety profile of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have increased since the 2023 European Medicines Agency (EMA) and U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) reviews.
criteria.R: Antineoplastic drugs are effective for malignant tumours, but they frequently cause severe adverse drug reactions (ADRs), which seriously affect treatment continuity and patient prognosis.
criteria.S: With the widespread use of novel therapeutic agents, an increasing number of drugs have been confirmed to be associated with interstitial lung disease (ILD).
criteria.T: The increasing use of calcineurin inhibitors (CNIs) among pregnant women highlights the importance of continuous safety surveillance. This study aimed to characterize the real-world safety signals of cyclosporine (CsA) and tacrolimus (TAC) during pregnancy using data from the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database.
criteria.U: Vaccine pharmacovigilance is critically important to ensure transparent information related to vaccine safety. We conducted a prospective, non-interventional, population-based cohort study, SafeVac2.0, in order to supplement passive surveillance of COVID-19 vaccines by collecting self-reported adverse events (AEs).
criteria.V: This pharmacovigilance study analyzed echinocandin-related adverse events (AEs) using the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database to identify agent-specific safety signals and inform clinical decision-making.
criteria.W: Sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulators are used for immune-mediated diseases, and macular oedema is an established ocular adverse effect. However, ocular-focused, class-wide postmarketing reporting across all five approved agents remains incompletely characterized.
criteria.X: Natural products represent an important source of candidates for breast cancer therapy. Here, we investigated the antitumor activity of (E)-4-(1-epoxy-7,8-propen)phenylbenzoate (CV2), a phenylpropanoid isolated from Croton velutinus roots, in MCF-7 breast cancer cells and evaluated its toxicity profile in nontumor cells and zebrafish embryos.
criteria.Y: Androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) are widely used across prostate cancer disease states, but spontaneous-report safety signals may be distorted by co-administered therapies.
criteria.Z: Mitotane remains the cornerstone of adrenocortical carcinoma. However, its real-world safety profile is poorly defined.
criteria.AA: Cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) inhibitors play an important role in the treatment of breast cancer and show therapeutic potential for gastrointestinal (GI) tumors.
criteria.AB: Alectinib is the standard first-line therapy for treatment-naïve ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Given its increasing clinical utilization, a comprehensive pharmacovigilance evaluation of its adverse events (AEs) is warranted.
criteria.AC: Imipenem/cilastatin is an important carbapenem antibiotic widely used for the treatment of severe infections and those caused by multidrug-resistant bacteria.
criteria.AD: Using the NSW Drug Misuse and Trafficking Act 1985 Schedule 1 of prohibited plants or prohibited drugs as an example of legislation that may be difficult for a computer search engine to resolve, an approach to produce valid chemical names and identifiers from the schedule entries is described and implemented.
criteria.AE: Pharmacovigilance and suspected adverse drug reaction (ADR) reporting are key components of patient safety and post-marketing drug surveillance. Spontaneous reporting systems concern suspected reactions, because causality is not established at the time of reporting.
criteria.AF: Drink-driving remains a leading global cause of road traffic fatalities. In Italy, the determination of blood alcohol concentration (BAC) in injured drivers relies on coordination between law enforcement and emergency departments (ED) to ensure legally admissible evidence.

questions.instructions:
Title of a research article: Dyslipidemia and Kidney Stone Risk: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Therapeutic Considerations

Each option below is the beginning of the abstract of an article from the same subject area (Pulmonary and Respiratory Medicine). Which option is the beginning of this article's abstract?

criteria.A: Anatomical variations in the Circle of Willis (CoW) may influence cerebral collateral pathways and the interpretation of vascular imaging. This study characterized their prevalence and clinical associations in a Turkish computed tomography angiography (CTA) cohort using complementary patient-level and component-level classifications.
criteria.B: Patients with acute right heart failure or pulmonary hypertension require cautious resuscitation because the right ventricle is highly preload-sensitive and has a narrow therapeutic window; both hypovolemia and volume overload may worsen hemodynamics.
criteria.C: We aimed to describe the clinical, laboratory, and radiological characteristics of children with complicated pneumonia/empyema who underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and to identify factors associated with length of hospital stay.
criteria.D: The rare HOXB13 G84E variant is one of few established high‐risk prostate cancer (PrCa) variants, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms by which it drives tumor development remain unknown.
criteria.E: Glucocorticoids (GCs) remain the cornerstone of polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) management, but their cumulative toxicity necessitates effective GC-sparing strategies.
criteria.F: Acute type A aortic dissection is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency characterized by sudden onset, severe pain, and high mortality, exerting profound physical and psychological burdens on affected individuals.
criteria.G: Cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) are established and emerging drug targets in cancer. Clinical success of CDK4/6 inhibitors in HR+/HER2- breast cancer has validated the CDK family therapeutically and stimulated development of both next-generation cell-cycle CDK inhibitors and inhibitors targeting transcriptional CDKs (CDK7-9, CDK11–13 and CDK19).
criteria.H: Osteosarcoma is an aggressive primary bone malignancy affecting both humans and dogs, and canine osteosarcoma represents a valuable comparative model for investigating novel therapeutic strategies.
criteria.I: Takayasu arteritis is a rare, chronic large-vessel vasculitis that primarily affects young women, particularly the aorta and its branches. It is traditionally regarded as an isolated vascular disease, and its coexistence with other systemic autoimmune diseases is uncommon, having been described mainly in case reports and small series.
criteria.J: We assessed whether an FDA-cleared quantitative CT (qCT) tool (Brainomix, e-Lung) identifies progressive pulmonary fibrosis (PPF) earlier than routine clinical diagnosis and evaluated the prognostic value of baseline and serial imaging biomarkers.
criteria.K: We report a case of giant hypervascular atypical lipomatous tumor/well-differentiated liposarcoma (ALT/WDLPS) of the cervicodorsal region in a 62-year-old man.
criteria.L: Real-world initial treatment strategies in SSc-PAH remain incompletely described. We aimed to characterise these strategies across haemodynamic thresholds and risk strata and evaluate outcome associations.
criteria.M: Carotid geometry and local hemodynamics are closely associated with atherosclerosis, yet how anatomy and disturbed flow jointly mark disease presence and relate to pro-atherogenic flow in still-non-stenosed bifurcations remains unresolved.
criteria.N: Lung cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, including among patients diagnosed with potentially curable disease. Current decisions regarding perioperative treatment and follow-up rely on a limited number of established prognostic factors.
criteria.O: The MUC5B rs35705950 polymorphism is the strongest common genetic risk factor for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), whereas its role in fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis (fHP) remains incompletely characterized, particularly in Eastern European cohorts.
criteria.P: The decision to administer surfactant therapy to preterm newborns is typically based on clinical respiratory findings, oxygen requirements, and the level of respiratory support.
criteria.Q: Event-free survival (EFS) is widely used in soft tissue sarcoma (STS) research but combines clinically distinct outcomes such as local recurrence (LR), distant metastasis (DM), and death into a single endpoint.
criteria.R: The study presents a rigorous evaluation of Tanacetum balsamita as a natural intervention for urolithiasis, a chronic condition characterized by high recurrence rates specifically, a 50% relapse rate within five years and 80% within ten years.
criteria.S: The closer a cancer model simulates the natural tumour environment, the more likely is a new therapeutic approach tested in this environment to succeed in clinical trials.
criteria.T: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) remains a major complication of prematurity, particularly among infants requiring prolonged respiratory support. Despite its clinical relevance, data on BPD epidemiology and risk factors in Kazakhstan are limited.
criteria.U: Isolated internal iliac artery aneurysm (IIAA) is rare and carries a high mortality when ruptured. Management is particularly challenging in very elderly, anticoagulated patients in whom open repair may carry substantial perioperative risk.
criteria.V: The prevalence of kidney stone (KS) disease and cardiometabolic diseases are simultaneously increasing in the United States. Dyslipidemia has been associated with an increased risk for KS formation and recurrence due to alterations in metabolism of purine and oxalate along with a defective urinary acidification mediated through insulin resistance.
criteria.W: A 7-month-old, 3.6-kg, intact male Dachshund was presented with a lifelong history of chronic respiratory signs. Multiple courses of antimicrobial therapy resulted in partial or complete clinical improvement, followed by recurrence after treatment discontinuation.
criteria.X: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-based systemic therapies were recently introduced to adjuvant management of renal cell carcinoma (RCC) in patients at high risk of recurrence.
criteria.Y: Complicated urinary tract infection associated with urinary stone disease remains clinically challenging because obstruction, infected stones, delayed microbiological confirmation, and antimicrobial resistance may converge in the same patient.
criteria.Z: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a major global health burden, affecting 300–400 million people worldwide and ranking as the fifth leading cause of death in the United States.
criteria.AA: Supine percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) has gained attention as a viable alternative to the traditional/historical prone approach for the treatment of large renal stones.
criteria.AB: Ferroptosis is a distinct form of regulated cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation and oxidative membrane damage, and it differs fundamentally from apoptosis, necroptosis, and pyroptosis in its molecular mechanisms and execution pathways.
criteria.AC: Oscillometry has been recognized as a non-invasive method for assessing respiratory conditions and is increasingly being implemented in routine clinical practice.
criteria.AD: Osteosarcoma, the most common primary bone malignancy in children and adolescents, frequently metastasizes to the lung, with a five-year survival rate of about 20% after lung metastasis.
criteria.AE: Despite the global availability and utilization of robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP), it remains a technically complex operation, with wide variation in training paradigms, surgical technique, and perioperative management.
criteria.AF: Nephrolithiasis is linked to chronic kidney disease (CKD), and diabetic patients may be at higher risk for renal decline. However, the interaction of diabetes, stone composition, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) trajectory in patients with nephrolithiasis remains underexplored, particularly in community-based populations.

questions.instructions:
A journal article is titled "Artificial learning: how sessional academics view contract cheating and digital academic misconduct in assessment".

Only one of the following abstract openings comes from that article; the others come from other recent articles in Safety Research. Which one is it?

criteria.A: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) for psychiatric diagnostic aid during clinical triage and mental health assessment has a potential value that is hard to underestimate.
criteria.B: Artificial intelligence (AI)-supported online proctoring is increasingly used in online and distance education, although its implementation continues to raise questions about anxiety, privacy, fairness, and technical reliability.
criteria.C: When Subini Annamma described a new theory, DisCrit (2013), she changed the course of what is possible from a scholarly and practical perspective for disabled people in higher education.
criteria.D: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly embedded in decisions that affect health, employment, housing, justice, and social policy. Rather than neutral tools, they reflect the data on which they are trained, the objectives they optimize, and the contexts in which they operate, reinforcing and amplifying existing social inequalities.
criteria.E: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence into scientific research has raised worries about scientific ethics and research integrity. This research offers a thorough bibliometric analysis.
criteria.F: According to the 2025 Student Well-being Pulse Report released by the IC3, which conducted a nationwide survey of 8,515 Indian high school students, nearly half have never received structured career counselling, and 1 in 6 Grade 12 students cite career uncertainty as their top stressor.
criteria.G: Adolescence is a critical developmental period during which physical fitness, executive function, and psychological resilience are closely interconnected.
criteria.H: For young people with a learning disability, transitioning to adulthood is a complex process, frequently resulting in limited choice and poor life outcomes.
criteria.I: Human societies rely on rules to coordinate behaviour, sustain cooperation and maintain social order. Yet compliance can be fragile when rules are weakly enforced and individuals observe others violating them.
criteria.J: Career adaptability is an important psychosocial resource that helps college students prepare for academic demands, employment uncertainty, and the transition from university to work.
criteria.K: Machines do not have emotions, but they can be programmed to express (to appear to have) certain emotions. In medicine, robots and AI machines are used that could express positive emotions (joy, compassion, hope, gratitude, inspiration or awe) and priorities.
criteria.L: Adolescents return to foster care for reasons that differ from younger children, yet little research has examined whether these reentries reflect newly reported maltreatment or ongoing behavioral health and family functioning challenges.
criteria.M: Academic misconduct predisposition remains an important concern in higher education, and peer behavior perception has emerged as a relevant correlate of students' academic integrity-related tendencies.
criteria.N: Ubuntu has emerged as the dominant African ethical vocabulary in global AI ethics, frequently invoked as a relational alternative to Western individualism.
criteria.O: Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT have been widely adopted by chemistry undergraduate university students as a learning tool, but few methods exist to measure the scope of their influence on essay writing.
criteria.P: The rapid ascent of decentralized prediction platforms such as Polymarket signals more than a regulatory or financial controversy.
criteria.Q: Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents can compound early errors across long trajectories. Existing safeguards mainly verify outcomes after execution or store unvalidated reflections; they do not provide an auditable pre-action policy that jointly controls risk, irreversibility, and cost.
criteria.R: AI tools, including chatbots, have become increasingly mainstream and could pose many problems for disabled people and their allies. Such problems could include the lack of accessibility of AI tools for disabled people, including disabled activists and disabled people as digital citizens.
criteria.S: Inroduction At present, school‑aged children face three common public‑health concerns: functional postural abnormalities, poor physical fitness, and visual fatigue accompanied by early refractive changes.
criteria.T: This paper critically examines social inclusion for learners with profound and multiple learning disabilities, arguing that models of educational inclusion inadequately capture their lived experiences.
criteria.U: This study investigated sessional academics’ perceptions of student misconduct in tertiary education assessments, focusing on contract cheating, misuse of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and unauthorised use of smart devices.
criteria.V: This study examined digital imperialism and its contribution to global inequality, focusing on the activities of Facebook, Cambridge Analytica, Bell Pottinger, and TikTok in Nigeria.
criteria.W: Positive psychology increasingly recognizes that wellbeing depends on meaningful social and organizational contexts, yet residential disability services are rarely examined as environments that structure the practical opportunities through which autonomy, competence, relatedness, agency, and social inclusion can develop.
criteria.X: The growing use of Computer-Aided Design (CAD) software in engineering education has reshaped assessment practices, creating new challenges for academic integrity.
criteria.Y: Artificial intelligence, after the boom of generative AI, is beginning to shape environmental decision-making, at the same moment that environmental justice (EJ) communities face intensifying ecological harm, federal disinvestment, and data erasure.
criteria.Z: The accelerating evolution of digital infrastructures and cognitive technologies has fundamentally reshaped contemporary social fabrics; a complex matrix of systemic opportunities and ethical challenges.
criteria.AA: This study aims to examine how artificial intelligence (AI) can be governed to advance educational justice, inclusion and ethical digital learning. It addresses incomplete integration across AI-in-education, AI-governance and educational-justice scholarship by developing a justice-oriented governance framework.
criteria.AB: This study develops and empirically validates a Corporate Ethical and Responsible AI (CERAi) lifecycle framework. The framework comprises three interdependent stages: design and development, testing and training, and deployment and usage.
criteria.AC: The digital economy is reshaping talent development needs and programme and curriculum provision in higher education, making sustained alignment between programme provision and societal needs an important concern for sustainable higher education.
criteria.AD: This paper introduces a thought experiment in reverse alignment, in which, instead of aligning artificial intelligence (AI) with human values, we examine how humans inadvertently align with AI systems.
criteria.AE: Previous research has found positive associations between physical activity and leisure-time sport participation and subjective well-being among children and adolescents.
criteria.AF: This study examines whether the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) in Italian companies is accompanied by organisational capacities to identify and mitigate bias in marketing and communication.

questions.instructions:
Removal of VirD2 from a synthetic T-DNA complex of Agrobacterium by the host DNA repair protein TDP2

questions.instructions:
“They’re just shifting a problem”: A qualitative study of stakeholder perceptions of the welfare implications of UK rescue dog importation

questions.instructions:

criteria.E: Tribal nations across the United States face disproportionate flood impacts yet remain significantly underrepresented in national‐scale assessments, creating a critical equity gap in climate adaptation.
criteria.F: The South Pacific Convergence Zone (SPCZ) is the dominant perennial rainfall feature of the Southern Hemisphere, yet the physical mechanisms driving its variability on decadal to multidecadal time‐scales are poorly understood.
criteria.G: The emergence of mission-oriented climate policy marks an important shift from traditional environmental governance towards transformative societal change.
criteria.H: The Atlantic Multidecadal Variability (AMV) influences North Atlantic sea surface temperatures and regional climate phenomena such as European droughts and hurricane activity.
criteria.I: A hybrid framework named “TRR–LSTM–TRR” is developed to reconstruct and predict 137 Cs activity concentrations in surface seawater of China’s coastal seas.
criteria.J: Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) marine survival has declined markedly over the past five decades, leading to concerns about future population viability.
criteria.K: Establishing protected areas (PAs) in the right locations is essential for the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework’s 30% target, yet existing PA networks are often misaligned with conservation needs.
criteria.L: Subalpine conifer forests in South Korea are increasingly exposed to climate-related stress, yet simple and repeatable field criteria for describing tree decline remain limited.
criteria.M: Climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of heatwaves, with profound consequences for forest carbon cycling. criteria.O: Given the rapid acceleration of the climate crisis, the IPCC has deemed Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) technologies as unavoidable to sufficiently mitigate the crisis.
criteria.P: Rising global population and living standards are increasing energy demand and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, intensifying the need for a sustainable energy transition.

criteria.S: Traditional dust emission schemes typically rely on photosynthetic vegetation (PV) alone when parameterizing key surface properties.

criteria.Y: Precipitation in low clouds affects cloud responses to aerosol perturbations, thereby impacting aerosol radiative forcing of climate, a significant but indeterminate contribution to uncertainty in future warming.
criteria.Z: Deforestation, as one of the most pressing global environmental challenges, can intensify local temperature extremes through altering surface properties (e.g. albedo, roughness and evapotranspiration) and the associated land–atmosphere interactions.

criteria.AB: Climate change is expected to alter climate conditions and increase the frequency and intensity of climate extremes, with implications for hydrological systems.
criteria.AC: Forest carbon projects have become increasingly relevant for climate mitigation, yet integrated evidence regarding their territorial distribution, governance arrangements, carbon-market performance, and environmental integrity remains limited in Peru.
criteria.AD: The Amazon biome faces intensifying threats to its biodiversity, including accelerated deforestation, overexploitation of wildlife, fires, agricultural expansion, mining, and infrastructure construction.

questions.instructions:
Here is the title of a recently published study: Navigating Identity and Well-Being: Intersectional Experiences of LGBTQ+ Youth in Eswatini Within Cultural, Legal, and Social Contexts

Below are 32 candidates, each the start of a published abstract from the same research area. Which candidate starts the abstract of this study?

criteria.A: LGBTQ+ youth in Eswatini navigate identity and well-being within social environments shaped by cultural expectations, legal restrictions, family relationships, educational institutions, and community attitudes.
criteria.B: Existing studies have primarily examined how biogenetic explanations for the causes of mental illness influence stigma, while largely neglecting the impact of presenting psychiatric medication or medical techniques as the primary solutions.
criteria.C: The present study examined how impairments in personality functioning relate to psychological well-being among LGBTQ+ individuals, with particular attention to the serial mediating roles of health literacy and experienced and anticipated sexual stigma in healthcare services.
criteria.D: Since 2018, adults in India have been able to engage in same-sex intimacy legally following the decriminalization of homosexual acts. Yet legal decriminalization alone does not determine how the press covers queerness in India, or what that coverage reveals about the cultural contours of LGBTQ+ identities in a rapidly changing country.
criteria.E: Organizations increasingly invest in adopting digital technologies to improve efficiency and competitiveness. Yet, in the post-adoption phase, these benefits depend on continued employee–technology interaction in everyday work, which can shape employee work and wellbeing and thereby influence organizational performance.
criteria.F: The rising yet underdiagnosed prevalence of mental disorders among young adults, due to stigma, limited knowledge, and reduced help-seeking, underscores the need for culturally validated tools to measure and enhance mental health literacy.
criteria.G: Although it is thought likely that clinical supervision places relational and emotional demands on the supervisor, supervisors' emotional and interpersonal experiences when delivering supervision are not well understood.
criteria.H: Families seeking gender-affirming treatment have described the importance of information regarding service procedure and expectations of treatment timelines.
criteria.I: The aim of the current study is to examine the relationships among bullying victimization, school safety, school belonging, teacher support, and emotional well-being using data from the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) 2022 with 135,348 adolescents across 15 education systems.
criteria.J: Large language models are increasingly used for informal mental health support, yet their safety during escalating suicide-risk conversations may depend on how prior information is presented.
criteria.K: Anthropomorphic robots are increasingly prominent technologies, yet how variations in robot gaze are associated with human perception and visual engagement remain poorly understood.
criteria.L: Burnout among nurses threatens healthcare quality and workforce sustainability. criteria.M: The present survey study (Prolific sample, N = 361) aimed to clarify relationships among age and socioemotional well-being as they pertain to chatbot use and perception by sampling across two age cohorts: emerging adults (18–24 years) and middle-aged adults (48–54 years).
criteria.N: Violence against LGBTIQA+ individuals is not limited to discrete acts of aggression. It also constitutes a territorial ecology that unevenly distributes habitability, safety, and recognition.
criteria.O: Parental expectations play a key role in shaping adolescents’ health behaviors, yet the mechanisms linking them to exercise behavior remain insufficiently understood.
criteria.P: Artificial systems increasingly participate in organizational work as recurrent contributors to interdependent activity, yet research remains fragmented across system capabilities, individual responses, episodic interactions, and constructs derived from human-only teams.
criteria.Q: The potential of artificial intelligence (AI) agents to engage in emotional conversations with humans is attracting increasing attention. Previous studies suggested that conversational agents powered by large language models such as ChatGPT can engage in emotionally competent conversations with humans.
criteria.R: As digital technologies permeate every corner of academic life, post-secondary students find themselves navigating an escalating tide of screen-mediated demands that blur boundaries between study, social connection, and rest.
criteria.S: Mental health literacy (MHL) plays an important role in the recognition, prevention, and management of mental disorders, but its current status among Chinese young adults and its potential moderating role in the association between anxiety and depression remain underexplored.
criteria.T: Traditional sports and games (TSGs) represent an important component of intangible cultural heritage (ICH), reflecting local traditions, cultural identities, and forms of social interaction transmitted across generations.
criteria.U: This study explores how students develop, negotiate and represent their mental health alongside their professional identities. The aim is to understand how nursing students construct and negotiate their mental health identities in academic and clinical environments.
criteria.V: The study investigated the influence of stress management on teachers’ job performance in public senior secondary schools in Bwari Area Council F.C.T.
criteria.W: This analysis unpacks how interstate conflicts change the scope and function of memory laws. Following diplomatic ruptures, memory entrepreneurs deploy conflict-time memory laws to essentialize adversaries, cause them reputational damage, and communicate specific interpretations of the conflict to both domestic and international audiences.
criteria.X: Office work is characterized by prolonged sitting and may be accompanied by musculoskeletal symptoms and reduced well-being.
criteria.Y: Driving frequently exposes individuals to conditions triggering acute stress, but its effects on drivers' visual behaviour remain insufficiently understood.
criteria.Z: Sexual well-being is integral to health, yet social responses to mental health conditions and sexual and gender diversity may restrict expression, safety, and belonging.
criteria.AA: Strong evidence shows that gratitude enhances well-being, though the mechanisms driving these effects are unclear. Here, we test the idea that gratitude may enhance well-being by (1) attuning people to the support that they receive and boosting perceptions of social support and (2) promoting support provision.
criteria.AB: Patients with major depressive disorder (MDD) have a substantially higher risk of suicide than the general population, whereas current suicide risk identification mainly relies on clinical interviews and standardized rating scales, with limited objectivity and capacity for continuous monitoring.
criteria.AC: Cyberbullying constitutes an increasing risk factor for adolescents’ psychological well-being, with teachers playing a pivotal role in both prevention and intervention efforts.
criteria.AD: Gender-affirming voice training (GAVT) has reduced gender incongruence for transgender and gender-nonconforming (TGNC) individuals, but remains limited by cost and scarcity of specialized providers.
criteria.AE: Perceptions of virtuous persons represent an important yet understudied dimension of moral cognition that may be associated with individuals' psychological functioning as well as their developmental and contextual experiences.
criteria.AF: Sexual minority youth (SMY) scholarship has lagged in its attention to the conceptual and practical distinctions between peer victimization and bullying.

questions.instructions:
Here is the title of a recently published study: Subject-Aware Detection of Depression from Wrist Actigraphy Using Per-Subject Distributional Aggregation and Interpretable Biomarker Analysis

Below are 32 candidates, each the start of a published abstract from the same research area. Which candidate starts the abstract of this study?

criteria.A: Vision–Language Navigation (VLN) requires embodied agents to interpret natural-language instructions in 3D environments.
criteria.B: High-dimensional image data often contain redundant pixel-level information, leading to increased computational complexity and reduced learning efficiency in machine learning models.
criteria.C: The Dynamic Window Approach (DWA) evaluates candidate motions for local robot navigation. This paper presents an Improved Dynamic Window Approach (IDWA) with two changes to trajectory evaluation.
criteria.D: In recent years, many regions have invested significant efforts in the in-depth study of artistic visual effects in urban environments to enhance the aesthetic appeal of urban districts.
criteria.E: To address issues in real-time fish monitoring, this study proposes a fish detection model based on YOLOv11, termed YOLO-Fish. The model focuses on optimizing the core feature extraction module C3k2 and reconstructing it with lightweight backbone networks.
criteria.F: RGB-infrared (RGB-IR) object detection combines visible appearance cues with infrared thermal information and supports perception under complex illumination, weak texture, occlusion, and large scale variation.
criteria.G: Deepfake video detection can benefit from multiple forensic cues, but the resulting responses are not always equally reliable or directly comparable. Moreover, informative forgery evidence may be concentrated in only part of a video.
criteria.H: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR) in educational technology has opened new opportunities for enhancing constructivist learning, particularly in computer network education.
criteria.I: In this article, a novel 4D Non-monotonic Sinusoidal Chaotic Map (NSCM) for confusion and a deep network-guided key map generation for diffusion are introduced to improve information security against various attacks.
criteria.J: High-throughput spatial transcriptomics technologies such as MERFISH and Stereo-Seq generate massive brain sections requiring accurate registration to 3D reference atlases.
criteria.K: Large model sparsity methods improve inference efficiency by removing unimportant weights, but existing methods are often affected by significant accuracy degradation and typically require sparsity‐aware fine‐tuning to restore accuracy.
criteria.L: The generalisability of AI-Generated Content (AIGC, e.g., images and videos) detection can be decomposed into two tightly coupled subspaces: a semantic subspace and a forgery subspace.
criteria.M: Patient-specific dressings for diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) must follow the individual lesion, yet pub- lished image-to-fabrication pipelines rely on depth sensing and seldom report the accuracy of the fabricated object.
criteria.N: Driven by the advancement of intelligent security, person re-identification has evolved from single-modality imagery to complex multimodal tasks involving infrared, text, sketches, and paintings.
criteria.O: Object detection has evolved dramatically over three decades, transitioning from handcrafted features to deep learning, transformers, and now large language models.
criteria.P: Airfield ground lighting is safety-critical electrical infrastructure and requires reliable inspection. We benchmarked lamp detection, colour assignment and embedded execution using 59 GoPro HERO 8 recordings acquired through scientific cooperation with Poznań-Ławica Airport.
criteria.Q: Real-world motion blur exhibits complex, spatially varying characteristics that challenge existing deblurring methods. While multi-stage architectures offer progressive refinement, simple inter-stage interactions often limit effective information transfer.
criteria.R: In adverse weather conditions such as fog, haze, rain, and snow, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) small object detection faces decreased accuracy due to reduced image quality and blurred object features, which seriously affects the reliability of low-altitude detection tasks.
criteria.S: Maritime logistics relies on documents that combine dense multilingual text, irregular layouts, and task-specific output schemas, requiring operational systems to recover text, structure, location, and semantics.
criteria.T: Segmentation of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can be used in the clinical care of patients with (suspected) Wilms tumor (WT). Manual segmentation, however, is time consuming and user dependent.
criteria.U: Traditional human activity recognition systems in wearable technologies typically separate sensing modalities, using mechanical sensors for motion detection and biophysical sensors such as electrocardiography for health monitoring.
criteria.V: Object detection in remote sensing scenarios faces multiple challenges, primarily manifested in multi-scale objects, class imbalance, densely packed small targets, and occlusion.
criteria.W: For small robots, annotation can outlast computation as a bottleneck: hardware is bought once, labels at every deployment. We study label efficiency for landmark detection on a humanoid soccer robot.
criteria.X: Detection of abnormal campus behavior is challenging because abnormal targets often exhibit large scale variations, small spatial extensions, frequent occlusions, complex background interference, and strong dependencies on relative spatial relationships.
criteria.Y: Automatic reading of analog pointer meters is affected by complex backgrounds, illumination changes, and camera viewpoints.
criteria.Z: This study evaluates the eleven visual tracking algorithms available in OpenCV for tracking hand-drawn markers on deforming human faces.
criteria.AA: We propose JEPADepth, a self-supervised monocular depth estimation framework that augments photometric view synthesis with an auxiliary masked-prediction loss computed in the representation space of a pretrained DINOv3 Vision Transformer (ViT), following the Image Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (I-JEPA) principle.
criteria.AB: Biomechanical event detection is fundamental to human movement analysis in clinical, rehabilitation, and sports settings, yet conventional laboratory systems remain costly and inaccessible in many contexts.
criteria.AC: To address the issues of easy loss and inaccurate localization of distant small targets in railway LiDAR point cloud foreign object detection, this paper proposes a 3D object detection method named RailMASDet.
criteria.AD: Depression is a widespread mental health disorder whose early diagnosis is often hindered by the reliance on subjective clinical assessments. This study proposes a subject-aware machine learning framework for detecting depression using wrist-worn actigraphy data, enabling continuous and objective monitoring of daily activity patterns.
criteria.AE: Cloud contamination in optical remote sensing imagery can obscure land-surface information and induce structural blurring and spectral shifts, thereby seriously affecting subsequent land-cover interpretation and quantitative analysis.
criteria.AF: Temporal Action Localization (TAL) aims to identify all action categories along with their precise temporal boundaries in untrimmed videos. It serves as a fundamental task supporting various downstream applications, including intelligent video editing, automatic summarization, anomaly detection, and human-computer interaction.

questions.instructions:
Find the abstract that matches a title.

Title: Oral Manifestations of Psoriasis: A Comprehensive Review of the Literature

All options are opening lines of abstracts from the field of Immunology. Which option opens the abstract of the work with the title above?

criteria.A: Inflammation and the balance between antitumor surveillance and immunoregulatory mechanisms influence chemically induced skin tumor development. STAT6 is a central mediator of IL-4/IL-13 signaling, but its contribution to early skin papilloma development remains unclear.
criteria.B: Bovine leukemia virus (BLV) causes a long subclinical infection and can result in B-cell leukemia/lymphoma. However, the in vivo relationship between expression of the BLV antisense transcript AS1 and the sense transcripts, tax/rex or env, and how these relate to host immune responses and lymphoma onset, remains unclear.
criteria.C: Sepsis-induced acute lung injury (SALI) is an important complication of sepsis associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, yet effective targeted therapies remain limited.
criteria.D: Macrophages sense viral double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) via the innate immune receptors TLR3 and MDA5 whose activation drives a robust inflammatory program, often coupled to cell death.
criteria.E: This narrative review examines therapeutic cancer vaccines, which have undergone a profound renaissance, transitioning from early peptide and dendritic cell-based formulations to next-generation mRNA platforms enabling personalized neoantigen targeting.
criteria.F: This study aims to systematically identify key hub genes in psoriasis pathogenesis through the integration of bioinformatics, machine learning and experimental validation methods.
criteria.G: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disease whose burden extends beyond the skin. Community-based data from Saudi Arabia are scarce, as most local studies recruit from dermatology clinics and miss people who never reach specialist care.
criteria.H: Brazil is among the world’s largest producers of Nile tilapia ( Oreochromis niloticus ), a species increasingly challenged by a complex of cocirculating pathogens that threatens production sustainability.
criteria.I: Despite improved survival, occupational challenges in with inborn errors of immunity (IEI) patients and their families remain unmeasured. We conducted a nationwide cross-sectional survey promoted by AIP and ImmunITA, including 420 IEI adults and 110 caregivers, integrating occupational data with patient-reported outcome measures.
criteria.J: White Spot Syndrome Virus (WSSV) remains a major factor limiting the sustainable development of crustacean aquaculture, creating an urgent need to develop comprehensive antiviral strategies with multiple protective functions.
criteria.K: Psoriasis is a common autoinflammatory disease driven by excessive IL-17 expression. While the pathomechanism of the disease has been revealed, epigenetic factors contributing to psoriasis are less well understood.
criteria.L: Severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bronchiolitis in infancy is associated with increased childhood asthma risk, but the mechanisms that sustain airway vulnerability remain unresolved.
criteria.M: Efficient generation of tumor-specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs) remains challenging. Although mRNA-based approaches enable the delivery and expression of diverse tumor-specific antigens, unmodified mRNA can trigger innate immune responses that suppress translation.
criteria.N: Influenza A virus (IAV) infection can progress from a localized respiratory illness to severe disease characterized by pulmonary inflammation, systemic cytokinemia, acute-phase responses and multi-organ pathology.
criteria.O: Dysregulated lipid metabolism is associated with psoriasis, but the HDL-related molecular traits linked to psoriatic disease remain incompletely defined.
criteria.P: Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) are important effectors of innate immunity but can contribute to inflammatory pathology when dysregulated. Although reactive oxygen species (ROS) are known to promote NET formation, the metabolic mechanisms that regulate NETosis remain incompletely understood.
criteria.Q: Icotrokinra, a targeted oral peptide that precisely blocks the interleukin-23 receptor, is approved to treat adult and pediatric (≥12 years, ≥40 kg) patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis (PsO).
criteria.R: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are key regulators of the breast tumor microenvironment and often display immunosuppressive functions that limit cellular immunotherapy efficacy.
criteria.S: The autoimmune regulator (AIRE) is essential for central immune tolerance, but its role in thymic epithelial cell (TEC) differentiation and development remains incompletely understood.
criteria.T: STING undergoes distinct post-translational modifications in autoimmune disorders, particularly in psoriasis. However, selectively targeting these disease-associated STING modifications remains a major therapeutic challenge.
criteria.U: Photobacterium damselae subsp. piscicida (Pdp) is one of the major bacterial pathogens affecting marine aquaculture worldwide. This study presents, to our knowledge, the first comparative genomic characterization of a Pdp strain (KLC25) isolated in Türkiye in the context of publicly available genomes from different geographic regions.
criteria.V: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated inflammatory disorder increasingly recognized as a systemic disease, yet the clinical significance and underlying mechanisms of its oral manifestations remain incompletely understood.
criteria.W: The thymic medulla provides the microenvironment for negative selection, late thymocyte maturation, and thymocyte egress, and is generally characterized by widespread distribution of medullary thymic epithelial cells (mTECs).
criteria.X: Oncogenic p53 mutant proteins not only promote cancer cell proliferation but also evade immune destruction for tumor progression. Besides hijacking immune checkpoints, p53 mutants in cancer cells may deactivate anticancer immune cells for evasion.
criteria.Y: Circulating T follicular regulatory (cTfr) cells are measured as blood biomarkers after vaccination, in autoimmune disease (e.g., lupus, rheumatoid arthritis) and cancer immunotherapy, yet whether they originate from natural Tregs (yielding nTfr) or germinal center T follicular helper (GC Tfh) cells (yielding iTfr) remains unknown.
criteria.Z: Plasma complement regulation during untreated HIV infection remains incompletely characterized. We examined complement markers in newly diagnosed, antiretroviral therapy (ART)-naive adults and their relationships with HIV RNA load.
criteria.AA: Psoriasis, long regarded as a chronic immune-mediated skin disorder, is now recognized as a systemic inflammatory disease linked to metabolic dysfunction.
criteria.AB: This study aims to investigate the role of insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA binding protein 3 (IGF2BP3) in the development of psoriasis, and to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms.
criteria.AC: The abundance of diverse naive CD8 + T cell clones is essential for broad protection against infection and cancer, but how sex and aging jointly shape this compartment remains poorly understood.
criteria.AD: Blood count-derived inflammatory indices have been proposed as accessible biomarkers of systemic inflammation in psoriasis, but their longitudinal behavior during selective interleukin-23 blockade remains uncertain.
criteria.AE: Very early onset inflammatory bowel disease (VEOIBD) is frequently driven by monogenic defects. Pathogenic variants in the syntaxin-binding protein 3 ( STXBP3 ) gene have been implicated in VEOIBD; however, the relationship between specific variant types and clinical manifestations remains incompletely understood.
criteria.AF: Tumor antigens provide the molecular interface between malignant transformation and host immunity, but their biological significance is determined by more than their molecular existence.

questions.instructions:
Title of a research article: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: spatial immune ecosystems, metabolic remodeling, and immunotherapeutic implications

Each option below is the beginning of the abstract of an article from the same subject area (Surgery). Which option is the beginning of this article's abstract?

criteria.A: Laparoscopic gastric plication (LGP) is a restrictive bariatric procedure that reduces gastric volume without resection and without the use of staplers or prosthetic materials.
criteria.B: Bladder urothelial carcinoma (BUC) exhibits high recurrence and poor prognosis, with limited efficacy of current immunotherapies. The role of the aggrephagy-related gene TUBA1A in the BUC immune microenvironment remains unclear.
criteria.C: This case describes hilar cholangiocarcinoma with pancreaticobiliary maljunction (PBM), pancreas divisum, and a type V right hepatic duct variant. Preoperative computed tomography (CT) with three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) clarified the complex ductal anatomy and informed reconstruction.
criteria.D: Heart transplantation (HTx) remains the definitive treatment for selected patients with advanced heart failure. The early post-transplant period is characterized by substantial morbidity and requires intensive surveillance.
criteria.E: Reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA) was designed for rotator cuff tear arthropathy but is now used in patients with an intact rotator cuff, most often for primary glenohumeral osteoarthritis (GHOA).
criteria.F: May-Thurner syndrome is a recognized cause of iliac vein thrombosis, but its role in recurrent distal deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is less well-defined.
criteria.G: Drug-coated balloon (DCB) therapy differs fundamentally from stent-based revascularization since the vessel itself becomes the treatment substrate. Consequently, vascular preparation is an important component of DCB therapy.
criteria.H: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is an aggressive liver malignancy characterized by pronounced cellular, spatial, and metabolic heterogeneity. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) are beginning to resolve this complexity by linking malignant, immune, stromal, and metabolic states to their tissue context.
criteria.I: Cefazolin is recommended for surgical prophylaxis in most patients with penicillin allergy labels (PALs) but concerns over beta-lactam cross-reactivity often limit use.
criteria.J: ABSTRACTBackground: Mandibular third molar surgery is often associated with pain that can cause considerable discomfort. Pre-emptive analgesia for the control of postoperative pain is targeted at preventing central sensitization before initiating surgical trauma.
criteria.K: Mesenchymal stromal-cell-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs) improve islet function, which may be mediated in part through the delivery of microRNAs (miRNAs) to β-cells.
criteria.L: Vacuolating cytotoxin A (VacA) is a critical virulence factor of Helicobacter pylori and is closely associated with chronic gastric diseases and gastric cancer.
criteria.M: To compare the effects of short-foot exercise (SFE) and toe-curl exercise (TCE) on movement control during single-leg landing in individuals undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR).
criteria.N: Maternal satisfaction is an important outcome of labour analgesia, reflecting pain relief and childbirth experience. This study compared maternal satisfaction and side-effect profiles following single-shot spinal labour analgesia using low-dose bupivacaine alone or with opioid adjuvants.
criteria.O: Supraspinatus fatty infiltration can occur without MRI-visible supraspinatus tear, but its relationship with acromioclavicular joint degeneration on shoulder MRI is unclear.
criteria.P: To report the clinical outcomes in a case of severe osteoarthritis secondary to patellectomy 40 years earlier and successfully treated with the function-preserving strategy via fibrous scar tissue extension in total knee arthroplasty (TKA) and postoperative rehabilitation program.
criteria.Q: The rising global prevalence of obesity has led to an increased demand for lipoabdominoplasty. Obesity is known to impair pulmonary function.
criteria.R: Pseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP) is a rare peritoneal malignancy most commonly originating from appendiceal mucinous neoplasms. Cytoreductive surgery (CRS) combined with has become the standard treatment for selected patients; however, evidence is largely based on retrospective single-centre series.
criteria.S: To compare functional recovery, pain patterns, analgesic requirements, and postoperative complications between patients with varus and valgus deformities who underwent primary total knee arthroplasty (TKA), and to evaluate the clinical impact of lower limb alignment on prognosis.
criteria.T: This study reports a case of conjoined twins in guinea pigs (Cavia porcellus) from the Peru breed, in the Cajamarca region, Peru.
criteria.U: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) has been associated with adverse metabolic outcomes, but its relationship with hepatic steatosis remains incompletely understood.
criteria.V: Intracranial germ cell tumors (GCTs) are a rare group of malignancies that are prone to recurrence and dissemination. The management of patients with multiple recurrent GCTs is particularly challenging.
criteria.W: Mesenteric venous thrombosis is an uncommon yet potentially life-threatening cause of mesenteric ischemia with an insidious clinical course. Delayed diagnosis of venous ischemia may lead to late complications such as bowel strictures, perforation, and fistulization.
criteria.X: Isokinetic testing is widely used after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR), but isolated knee strength may not reflect function during braking, re-acceleration, and stabilization.
criteria.Y: Neoadjuvant treatment has become an integral component of multidisciplinary management for resectable esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC).
criteria.Z: This study evaluated the association between lateral tibial slope (LTS), measured using the Hudek method on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) before primary anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) reconstruction, and ACL graft rerupture, and assessed the discriminative performance and reliability.
criteria.AA: Accurate assessment of volume status and fluid responsiveness is essential to guide fluid therapy, as unnecessary fluid administration may lead to fluid overload and adverse outcomes.
criteria.AB: The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-stimulator of interferon genes (STING) signaling pathway can recognize pathogen-derived and host DNA. This factor triggers innate immune responses and thereby establishes a broad and effective surveillance mechanism for tissue damage and pathogen invasion.
criteria.AC: Central nervous system germ cell tumors (CNS GCTs) are rare neoplasms that predominantly affect children and adolescents and exhibit striking geographic and demographic variation.
criteria.AD: Transplant-related pulmonary fibrosis (TPF) occurs after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplant and after lung transplantation. Effective therapies that prevent or reverse established transplant-related airway fibrosis remain limited.
criteria.AE: Heterogeneous responses across disease sites may occur after systemic therapy for biliary tract cancer (BTC), but their pathological and immune features remain poorly characterized.
criteria.AF: While immune dysfunction is recognized as pivotal in biliary atresia (BA) pathogenesis, comprehensive characterization of disease-specific immune cell subtypes and stromal components remains incomplete.

questions.instructions:
Article title: GPS-Synchronized System for FPGA-Based Acceleration Measurement

Which of these abstract beginnings belongs to the article with this title? The other options are taken from different articles in the same subfield.

criteria.A: Software-Defined Networking (SDN) simplifies network control by centralizing decisions in a controller, yet many deployments still depend on legacy Layer-2 behavior that was not designed for adversarial settings.
criteria.B: Over the years, TCP congestion control research has advanced through extensive algorithmic refinements.
criteria.C: Multi-UAV tracking can extend coverage by combining aerial observations with reports from fixed monitors and mobile sources. Intermittent links and heterogeneous sources nevertheless create delayed, duplicated, and unreliable evidence, while broad sharing consumes limited bandwidth and energy.
criteria.D: A Network Intrusion Detection System (network IDS or NIDS) is a widely used technology to enhance an organization’s security posture. A NIDS monitors the organizational network for cyber attacks, malware activity, and other malicious network traffic, raising alerts upon detecting such traffic.
criteria.E: We propose an enhanced phased decoding scheme and the corresponding hardware architecture based on persistent S-min candidate tracking for high-rate low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes of 50G passive optical networks (50G-PON).
criteria.F: This paper proposes an autonomous, resource-efficient, FPGA-based synchronization architecture for distributed accelerograph networks.
criteria.G: The rapid expansion of Internet of Things (IoT) deployments has increased the need for security approaches that combine data-driven threat detection with context-aware risk prioritisation.
criteria.H: Edge databases must coordinate replica freshness, consistency requirements, and governance restrictions despite intermittent connectivity. This study specifies an Edge-Aware Database Management System (EA-DBMS) architecture centered on the Policy-Aware Distributed Edge Catalog (PADEC).

criteria.A: Retinal vessel segmentation is essential for diagnosing eye diseases. However, complex multiscale vascular structures and low contrast make accurate segmentation difficult.

criteria.N: Accurate preoperative assessment of HER2 status is critical for guiding targeted therapy, but conventional biopsy-based methods are invasive and limited by tumor heterogeneity.
criteria.O: Keratoconus is a progressive corneal ectatic disorder characterized by stromal thinning and biomechanical weakening of the cornea, leading to progressive corneal protrusion and visual impairment.
criteria.P: Virtual reality (VR) is becoming increasingly popular in radiology, with a variety of diagnostic applications being tested. However, VR is yet to be tested in the context of MRI studies.
criteria.Q: T cell immunoglobulin and ITIM domain (TIGIT) is an immune checkpoint receptor expressed on T and NK cells that, upon interaction with its ligand CD155, suppresses immune cell activation.

criteria.V: Theranostic imaging agents combine molecular diagnosis, targeted therapy and monitoring of treatment response into a single paradigm of precision medicine.
criteria.W: The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the influence of perfusion pressure in postmortem computed tomography angiography (PMCTA) on the visualisation of the coronary arteries.
criteria.X: Corticosteroid injection is commonly used for moderate carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS), but factors associated with subsequent surgery remain unclear. This study evaluated baseline clinical, electrophysiological, and ultrasonographic factors associated with long-term surgery risk.
criteria.Y: Nanobodies are compact and stable proteins derived from the variable domain of camelid heavy-chain-only antibodies (VHH). Advances in structural biology, molecular modeling, and artificial intelligence (AI) are shifting VHH discovery from empirical selection toward data-driven design.
criteria.Z: Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint blockade, usually combined with platinum-based chemotherapy, has improved pathologic response and event-free survival in patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

criteria.AB: Antibody fusion proteins incorporating immunomodulatory molecules, such as cytokines of the common γ-chain receptor family and costimulatory members of the TNF superfamily, hold great potential for cancer immunotherapy, with many candidates already advancing into clinical studies.
criteria.AC: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of mortality worldwide. Among them, myocardial infarction (MI), which is characterized by abnormal myocardial motion, remains a critically important condition to detect.

questions.instructions:

Below are 32 candidates, each the start of a published abstract from the same research area. Which candidate starts the abstract of this study?

criteria.A: This study aims to investigate Theileria annulata infection in cattle herds in Thi-qar governorate and the Marshes. The 115 blood samples were collected from cattle of different ages and sexes in the Dhi-qar governorate and the marshes in Iraq.
criteria.B: Theileria annulata causes tropical theileriosis in cattle and is endemic in Kazakhstan. Although molecular diagnostic methods for this pathogen exist, data on its molecular surveillance and genetic diversity in Kazakhstan remain limited.
criteria.C: Hard tick infestation in cattle was investigated across seven agro-climatic zones of Gujarat, India, to determine prevalence, genus-level distribution, seasonal patterns, host- and management-associated factors, and farmer-reported control practices.

criteria.G: Microsporidia are obligate intracellular parasites that infect diverse animals. Budding yeast has long been used to define core molecular pathways and inhibitors that target them.
criteria.H: Canine babesiosis is a clinically significant tick-borne disease, caused by different Babesia species. Babesia canis, one of the most important and widespread species in Europe, is transmitted by Dermacentor reticulatus ticks and can cause potentially fatal canine disease.
criteria.I: Current strategies aim to eliminate schistosomiasis as a public health problem globally by 2030. As this target approaches, up-to-date knowledge of the burden and distribution of schistosomiasis is crucial.
criteria.J: Recently, several studies using cloned PCR amplicons have revealed greater haplotype diversity in Giardia duodenalis assemblage B than can be detected using conventional methods.
criteria.K: This study compared serological and molecular approaches for detecting Leptospira spp. using paired blood and urine samples from 124 asymptomatic stray dogs.
criteria.L: Neoehrlichia mikurensis and Borrelia miyamotoi are emerging tick-borne pathogens that primarily cause disease in immunocompromised individuals. Human co-infection with both pathogens has not previously been reported.
criteria.M: Cryptosporidium species are significant enteric parasites of cattle with zoonotic potential. criteria.O: Leptospirosis is a zoonotic infection that can cause acute liver injury and mimic viral hepatitis. criteria.R: Ticks (Acari: Ixodidae) are important ectoparasites and vectors of numerous pathogens affecting wildlife, domestic animals, and humans. Although birds play a significant role in tick ecology, information on tick infestations in wild galliform birds remains limited.
criteria.S: To describe the pivotal role of conventional B-mode and contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) in identifying and characterizing rare visceral manifestations of Bartonella henselae infection in an immunocompetent individual.
criteria.T: Ectoparasitic resistance is increasingly reported worldwide, with major implications for animal welfare and economic sustainability in production and companion animals.
criteria.U: Ticks are globally significant ectoparasites of livestock, transmitting pathogens and causing substantial economic losses. Their distribution is shaped by ecological, climatic, and host‑related factors, while control strategies face persistent challenges such as acaricide resistance and limited vaccine efficacy.
criteria.V: In China, sustained snail control, environmental management, and mass drug administration with praziquantel reduced schistosomiasis to near-elimination levels, yet re-emergence in Sichuan Province during the early 2000s exposed vulnerabilities in late-stage control.
criteria.W: Many people perceive spring water as a healthy alternative to tap water. However, unlike treated tap water, which undergoes rigorous filtration and disinfection, untreated or inadequately treated spring water may pose a higher risk of waterborne infections.
criteria.X: Helminth infections continue to present a substantial public health challenge worldwide, particularly in tropical and developing areas. Despite the widespread use of anthelmintic drugs for treatment and control, their effects on host cells remain poorly understood.
criteria.Y: Parasitic contamination of food sources, particularly vegetables, poses a persistent threat to public health globally, especially in developing countries where hygiene and sanitation are often inadequate.
criteria.Z: Pathogenic Leptospira transitions between environmental reservoirs and mammalian hosts, exposing the bacterium to distinct temperature conditions.
criteria.AA: Theileriosis is endemic in Central Asia; however, the geographic distribution and genetic diversity of Theileria spp. in livestock in Kazakhstan remain poorly characterized.
criteria.AB: Schistosomiasis is a parasitic neglected tropical disease that remains a major public health problem in many African countries. Accurate diagnosis is essential for control, surveillance and elimination efforts.
criteria.AC: In recent years, tick-borne viruses (TBVs) have gained significant prominence in public and veterinary health due to reports of fatal cases associated with vertebrates and the identification of a wide diversity of viruses in ixodid ticks through molecular techniques, particularly high-throughput sequencing.
criteria.AD: Sheep and cattle are considered maintenance hosts for Leptospira interrogans serovar Hardjo-prajitno and Leptospira borgpetersenii serovar Hardjo-bovis in Ireland, where the disease is endemic in these species.
criteria.AE: Cryptosporidium spp. and Giardia duodenalis are enteric protozoan parasites of veterinary and public health significance, yet molecular epidemiological data from Australian pig populations remain limited, and no study has previously been conducted in Victoria.

questions.instructions:
Here is the title of a recently published study: Early defoliation and nitrogen fertilization: effects on maize morphophysiology and production

Below are 32 candidates, each the start of a published abstract from the same research area. Which candidate starts the abstract of this study?

criteria.A: Maize–soybean strip intercropping is promoted in Southwest China to improve land use and diversify crop production, but maize hybrids vary in their ability to maintain yield under this system.
criteria.B: Development of automated ways to prepare udders before harvesting milk has allowed for more consistent application of procedures like disinfecting, stimulating, and drying, therefore replacing manual techniques.
criteria.C: Brown seaweed supplementation has attracted increasing interest as a nutritional strategy for mitigating enteric methane (CH 4 ) emissions in cattle while potentially supporting animal productivity and health.
criteria.D: Phenological responses of camelina to management were evaluated using days after planting (DAP) and cumulative growing degree days (GDD) at nine main BBCH stages.
criteria.E: Soil properties, fertilization, tillage, and straw management practices vary widely in the Mollisol region of Northeast China. criteria.I: Our objective was to evaluate the effects of oral administration of Paraclostridium bifermentans (PB) on production performance, metabolic responses, and ru-men function in multiparous Holstein cows.
criteria.J: Wheat production in desert environments is constrained by poor soil fertility, particularly limited nitrogen availability. Optimizing nitrogen fertilization and selecting well-adapted genotypes are therefore important for improving wheat productivity under desert farming conditions.
criteria.K: Dairy production contributes substantially to food security, employment and rural livelihoods, yet the economic performance of dairy enterprises in South Africa remains poorly documented.
criteria.L: Oat is a staple cereal in semi-arid regions and requires eco-friendly nitrogen management to stabilize yield and mitigate environmental risks.
criteria.M: Rapid decision-making during exotic animal disease outbreaks necessitates the early characterisation of transmission dynamics; however, in practice, a strategic balance between accuracy and speed is required.

criteria.P: Oil palm empty fruit bunches (OPEFB) are abundant lignocellulosic by-products with potential as ruminant feed, but their utilisation is limited by high fiber recalcitrance.
criteria.Q: The objective of this study was to evaluate the effect of foliar and soil application of molybdenum (Mo) fertilizer on the biological efficiency, competitive ability, and nutrient uptake of the sorghum–cowpea intercropping system.
criteria.R: This study investigated the effects of single or combined dietary supplementation with quercetin (QUE) and glucoraphanin (GRA) on growth performance, serum antioxidant capacity and biochemical parameters, rumen fermentation, and ruminal microbiota of meat sheep.

criteria.V: Early pregnancy diagnosis is essential for improving reproductive efficiency and reducing non-productive days in commercial swine production.
criteria.W: Our objective was to evaluate the effects of oral propylene glycol supplementation (PG; 300 mL) on the corpus luteum (CL) transcriptome of non-pregnant, non-lactating dairy cows.
criteria.X: Adverse meteorological conditions often force farmers to plant maize ( Zea mays L.) outside its optimal planting window. Early or delayed planting can significantly influence crop phenology, yield, and disease severity.
criteria.Y: Early-stage defoliation represents a mechanical stress with increasing relevance in intensive cropping systems. This study investigated the morphophysiological responses and compensatory capacity of maize subjected to early defoliation and nitrogen (N) top-dressing management.
criteria.Z: To identify the sowing window that jointly optimizes forage biomass and seed quality of Panicum maximum cv. C1 at Bouaké, Côte d’Ivoire.
