questions.instructions:
Title of a research article: Wearable Multi-Sensor Fusion for Field Assessment of Dynamic Postural Stability During the Curling Delivery in Young Adult Curlers: Integrating Trunk Kinematics, Plantar Pressure and Core-Muscle Activation

Each option below is the beginning of the abstract of an article from the same subject area (Physical Therapy, Sports Therapy and Rehabilitation). Which option is the beginning of this article's abstract?

criteria.A: The Timed Up and Go (TUG) test is widely used to assess mobility and fall risk in older adults, but total completion time does not capture phase-specific motor control.
criteria.B: Balance assessment in older adults is central to fall-risk evaluation and rehabilitation planning, yet widely used clinical tests such as the single-leg stance require postures most likely to provoke a fall.
criteria.C: Italy’s Law 234/2021 introduced specialist physical education (PE) teachers into grades 4–5 of primary school (ages 9–11), replacing exclusively generalist provision for the subject.
criteria.D: There is no measure that assesses self-perceptions of recovery in service members. This report describes the development and validation of the Military Illness and Injury Recovery Scale-17 (MIIRS-17) in a sample of active duty personnel.
criteria.E: Project-based learning (PBL) combines student-centred learning with motor practice, but evidence on physical activity and motor performance in school physical education remains limited.
criteria.F: To overcome the practical challenges of implementing differentiated instruction in large physical education (PE) classes, this study develops a composite stratification framework.
criteria.G: This cross-sectional study examined adjusted associations between learning motivation, parental support, and Physical Education, Sports, and Health (PJOK) achievement among Grade VII and VIII students at SMPN 2 Kras.
criteria.H: Generalized joint hypermobility (GJH) features ligamentous laxity and proprioceptive deficits, which impair balance. Traditional center of pressure (COP) metrics may not fully elucidate postural instability mechanisms.
criteria.I: Freezing of Gait (FOG) is a disabling feature of Parkinson’s disease (PD). However, the neural mechanisms underlying voluntary stopping impairments remain unclear.
criteria.J: Disability assessment determines access to social and healthcare support, yet the operation of assessment pathways may be shaped by policy implementation and facility capacity.
criteria.K: This study examined the associations between aerobic and muscular fitness and evaluated whether handgrip strength (HGS) could serve as a simple indicator of physical fitness, as determined by physical fitness tests, among Saudi girls aged 10 to 14 years.
criteria.L: To evaluate whether adding Baduanjin exercise to conventional physiotherapy improves balance, functional mobility, walking capacity, and motor signs compared with conventional physiotherapy alone in nursing-home residents with Parkinson’s disease.
criteria.M: Postural control in curling is expressed during a dynamic, sport-specific delivery on a single sliding leg, yet it is still assessed almost exclusively with static single-leg force-plate protocols that poorly reflect on-ice demands.
criteria.N: Drawing on a sociocultural conceptualisation of teachers' professional vision (PV), encompassing selective attention and knowledge-based reasoning, we foreground the social embeddedness of noticing and its relationship to power, equity and discrimination.
criteria.O: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a common complication of diabetes mellitus that may impair balance, mobility, and functional independence. Exercise using unstable surfaces, such as Wobble Board and Swiss Ball, may improve these functional outcomes.
criteria.P: Maintaining a stationary manual wheelchair wheelie is a highly demanding dynamic postural control task that can be biomechanically modeled as an inverted pendulum.
criteria.Q: University students face increasing psychological pressure, yet formal mental health services often remain limited in reach and depend on active help-seeking.
criteria.R: Inertial measurement units (IMUs) are increasingly used as portable tools for postural sway assessment, for which force platforms are the gold standard.
criteria.S: Intrinsic mechanisms and feedback control act together to stabilize the body in upright tasks. In unperturbed standing and walking, their combined effects can be captured by lumped stabilization models, relating delayed center of mass position and velocity information to current ground reaction forces.
criteria.T: Neurologic pathologic conditions, including traumatic brain injury (TBI), and natural aging often present with concurrent physical and cognitive challenges.
criteria.U: Dynamic stability during human movement reflects interactions among body configuration, support conditions, mechanical state, and short-term state evolution.
criteria.V: Age-related declines in lower-limb somatosensory function may contribute to impaired motor control and increased fall risk in older adults. Although plantar sensory stimulation has been reported to improve postural control, its effects on neural processing remain unclear.
criteria.W: Multiple sclerosis (MS) often leads to significant impairments in gait and mobility. Although walking braces are commonly prescribed, their real-world effectiveness is limited by insufficient adaptation.
criteria.X: This study aimed to quantify prefrontal cortex (PFC) activation and postural control complexity in older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) during single-task standing and dual-task standing balance conditions and to investigate the associations between these measures.
criteria.Y: Lower limb amputation (LLA) is a major surgical procedure that affects an individual’s physical, psychological, and social well-being. Effective rehabilitation through patient education is vital for improving independence and adaptation after amputation.
criteria.Z: Asymmetrical load carriage is a common component of daily activities. Carrying a backpack, handbag, or groceries on one side for example alters the center of mass of the system and may challenge postural stability.
criteria.AA: Although resistance training is increasingly promoted for adolescent health, it remains unevenly embedded in everyday physical education practice, and little is known about how school-based resistance training is positioned within Islamic secondary school contexts.
criteria.AB: Anticipatory postural adjustments (APA) generate initial center of mass motion during gait initiation and are associated with gait performance. While APA amplitude and duration have been linked to gait speed under single-task conditions, it remains unclear how these relationships are altered when motor control is constrained by cognitive demands.
criteria.AC: Sleep deprivation (SDEP) impairs cognitive control, which may affect movements that rely on these processes, such as walking. To test whether gait changes after one night of SDEP reflect reduced cognitive capacity, we compared its effects with those of dual-task walking (i.e. walking while performing a simultaneous cognitive task).
criteria.AD: This study aims to examine the impact of dual-task (DT) conditions on dynamic stability during stair ambulation in healthy young adults, with a specific focus on gender differences.
criteria.AE: People with multiple sclerosis have difficulties walking and show a high energy cost of walking. Balance problems may contribute.
criteria.AF: Single-leg landing protocols differ in task components. We estimated pattern differences in vertical time to stabilization (V-TTS) and the Dynamic Postural Stability Index (DPSI) at two individualized heights, with 95% confidence intervals, and tested whether they changed with height.

questions.instructions:
Here is the title of a recently published study: Integrated hydrogen system analysis across the resource-environment-economy nexus: a case study of China

Below are 32 candidates, each the start of a published abstract from the same research area. Which candidate starts the abstract of this study?

criteria.A: Rural agricultural regions such as the Chalan Beel area in Bangladesh often suffer from unreliable grid access, high diesel dependence, and the absence of predictive energy management.
criteria.B: Remote Arctic communities in Canada face significant challenges in transitioning from diesel-dependent energy systems to renewable alternatives. criteria.C: Stand-alone hydrogen production from cheap renewable power, notably solar, has received considerable attention as a way to produce fuel and feedstock for a future climate-neutral energy system.
criteria.D: Wind‐power fluctuations subject battery energy storage systems to frequent charge‐discharge cycling, thereby accelerating battery degradation and shortening battery lifetime.
criteria.E: Cold-climate dwellings can face coincident electricity and domestic hot-water shortfalls in winter, when solar availability is at its lowest.
criteria.F: Coupled photovoltaic-hydrogen (PV–H 2 ) plants are emerging as a cornerstone technology for large-scale green hydrogen production, and their reliable, safety-compliant operation is a prerequisite for the industrial deployment of renewable hydrogen at scale.
criteria.G: The article examines progress in the system integration of renewable energy sources in China over the period 2020–2026, focusing on the challenge of integrating rapidly expanding renewable energy capacity into the power system.
criteria.H: The increasing deployment of distributed energy resources is accelerating the transition toward sustainable and decentralised energy systems. In this context, Hydrogen Energy Communities (HECs) have emerged as a promising framework for integrating local energy generation, hydrogen production, storage, and consumption.
criteria.I: This study evaluates the techno-economic feasibility of offshore wind-based ammonia production in 2035 and 2050. A pseudo-dynamic modeling framework with capacity optimization is applied to three offshore sites in Colombia, Denmark, and Spain using long-term wind data to capture multidecadal wind variability.
criteria.J: This study develops a high-renewable hybrid microgrid integrating solar photovoltaic (PV), wind turbine (WT), and grid interaction for a university campus, with a distinctive focus on lifecycle emission performance.
criteria.K: This research explores the effect of higher penetration of variable renewables on energy fluctuations at various time scales and the necessity of energy storage systems for balancing power supply.
criteria.L: This study presents a province-level techno-economic and environmental assessment of integrated PV-based electricity, hydrogen, and freshwater production systems across 34 Afghan provinces.
criteria.M: Electrocatalytic organic oxidation coupled with hydrogen production can reduce energy demand while generating value-added chemicals, but its process-level economics and environmental impacts remain insufficiently evaluated.
criteria.N: The hydrogen industry requires an integrated decarbonization strategy that aligns supply-side optimization with demand-side growth to support effective policy design and long-term sustainability.
criteria.O: To achieve low-carbon and low-cost energy supply while meeting the dynamic electricity, heating, and cooling demands of residential communities, an integrated energy system combining solar energy and hydrogen energy is proposed.
criteria.P: Morocco’s National Green Hydrogen Roadmap targets large-scale hydrogen exports, yet the offshore wind and tidal resources of the Atlantic Sahara coast remain underexplored, and single-resource electrolysis plants suffer from low, variable electrolyser utilisation.
criteria.Q: Off-grid hybrid renewable energy systems (HRES) can supply electric-vehicle charging stations (EVCS) in grid-constrained regions, but storage sizing and battery operating stress must be evaluated on a consistent physical and economic basis.
criteria.R: Decarbonizing the steel industry is essential for achieving global net-zero emissions and fostering sustainable industrial systems. criteria.S: Low-carbon hydrogen investment appraisal metrics usually fail to capture the broader economic, environmental, and social impact.
criteria.T: This research work conducts an economic, operational, and environmental evaluation of a solar–wind–battery–hydrogen hybrid renewable energy generation system for a typical household in the Limpopo province of South Africa.
criteria.U: With the rapid development of the digital economy, the scale of data center computing power continues to expand, and the high-density, high load, and uninterrupted power supply demand puts forward extreme requirements for the dynamic response capability and power supply guarantee accuracy of the supporting energy storage system.
criteria.V: Hydrogen is increasingly recognized as a key energy carrier for supporting global decarbonization and achieving net‑zero emission targets by 2050. Canada has strong potential to become a major hydrogen producer and exporter due to its abundant renewable resources, existing energy infrastructure, and access to international markets.
criteria.W: Achieving global climate targets requires substantial reductions in greenhouse gas emissions, particularly in energy-intensive industries. Green hydrogen, produced via renewable-powered electrolysis, offers a promising decarbonisation pathway.
criteria.X: Hydrogen is a versatile energy carrier that can be produced from a range of feedstocks. Therefore, decentralized hydrogen production from renewable energy sources is gaining popularity worldwide, as it is considered environmentally friendly and less energy-intensive due to the use of cleaner energy sources and proximity to end-users.
criteria.Y: This study presents the design and dynamic assessment of an Energy Management System (EMS) for a standalone hybrid solar photovoltaic (PV) system integrating lithium-ion battery and green hydrogen storage technologies in Burkina Faso.
criteria.Z: In grid-connected PV-ESS plants, battery degradation is often treated as an external correction rather than a quantity coupled directly to sizing and dispatch decisions.
criteria.AA: Hydrogen is widely considered as a key option for decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors; however, identifying where and how it should be deployed requires system-level, multi-impact assessment to avoid environmental burden shifting.
criteria.AB: The integration of non-dispatchable renewable energy generators into small islands with autonomous electricity grids is by no means straightforward, as such systems cannot benefit from interconnections to mainland grids.

Each option below is the beginning of the abstract of an article from the same subject area (Cognitive Neuroscience). Which option is the beginning of this article's abstract?

criteria.A: Parkinson's disease exhibits heterogeneous spatiotemporal patterns of neurodegeneration. Dopaminergic therapy improves motor symptoms by modulating brain function in affected regions, yet whether the neural mechanisms through which dopaminergic therapy exerts its effects are linked to this heterogeneity of neurodegeneration remains unclear.
criteria.B: Motion-induced spatial conflict occurs when an isoluminant boundary moves smoothly near a moving luminance-defined boundary: observers perceive spatial jitter superimposed on the otherwise smooth trajectory, despite the absence of physical jitter.
criteria.C: Planning is critical for adaptive behaviour in a changing world, because it lets us anticipate the future and adjust our actions accordingly. While prefrontal cortex is crucial for this process, it remains unknown how planning is implemented in neural circuits.
criteria.D: Perceptual learning improves sensory sensitivity through practice but is typically specific to trained stimuli. Two contrasting accounts have been proposed: fine-tuning of feature-selective neurons in early sensory cortex, which raises a stability-plasticity dilemma, and reweighting of stable sensory inputs by higher-level readout.
criteria.E: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is increasingly characterized as a disorder of brain dynamics, but the temporal scale on which resting-state activity differs from healthy controls remains unclear.
criteria.F: Laterality, the preference for using one side of the body over the other, has been observed in various animal species, including frogs and toads.
criteria.G: Music can support social bonding, especially in face-to-face interactions, but its effects in online environments with reduced social cues are less understood.
criteria.H: Typical visual displays cover only a fraction of the visual field. How do such restrictions influence the perception of visual speed during self-motion?
criteria.I: Appetitive Pavlovian cues can drive maladaptive reward seeking via stimulus-reward memories. Disrupting memory reconsolidation offers a potential strategy to reduce their influence, but evidence for β-adrenergic blockade with propranolol is inconsistent across behavioural paradigms, particularly relative to NMDA receptor antagonism.
criteria.J: Patient-specific seizure prediction remains challenging because preictal EEG patterns and channel relevance vary substantially across individuals.
criteria.K: Accessing an autism diagnosis can be complex and protracted, shaped by interactions across education and health services. While the importance and challenges of autism diagnosis in the UK are well-documented, limited research examines how schools support families during this process.
criteria.L: Lexical-disambiguation tasks with supplied context do not reveal whether readers would choose to seek evidence before deciding. Therefore, we adapted the spatial T-maze in the active-inference package pymdp to show how agents seek and use contextual information under lexical uncertainty.
criteria.M: As the population of cochlear implant (CI) candidates and recipients grows, there is a need for more audiologists to meet their clinical needs. Little information exists regarding the perception of recent doctorate of audiology (AuD) graduates and the training they received related to CI.
criteria.N: Long-term sport participation has been associated with selective differences in temporal and perceptual-cognitive processing, but it remains unclear whether such differences extend to auditory-musical perception.
criteria.O: Task-based functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) examines how the brain dynamically responds to cognitive and perceptual demands, offering complementary insight beyond traditional activation-based analyses in schizophrenia.
criteria.P: Advances in naturalistic language assessment, portable neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and brain-network modeling are creating new opportunities to evaluate post-stroke aphasia under conditions closer to real-world communication.
criteria.Q: Beyond motor control, the cerebellum has increasingly been implicated in cognitive functions, including inhibitory control, whereas its contribution to feedback-based associative learning remains less well established.
criteria.R: A few studies have shown that brain catecholamines are implicated in language comprehension. However, the specific cognitive processes they modulate remain underexplored.
criteria.S: Visual memory is known to be influenced by objective image properties, including image size and contrast, as well as visual category. However, the influence of illusory perceptual experience on memory remains less understood.
criteria.T: Understanding how humans process visual information during learning remains a central challenge in cognitive neuroscience. Traditional approaches typically rely on behavioral observations or indirect neural measures, which limits direct insight into learners' internal cognitive representations.
criteria.U: It is generally accepted that emotions are represented more in the right than in the left hemisphere and that temporal and frontal brain structures play a prominent role in functions of representation and control of emotions.
criteria.V: This study investigates alterations in causal connectivity within resting-state brain functional networks in patients with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) using the Convergent Cross Mapping (CCM) method.
criteria.W: Sexual objectification is associated with viewing women in an object-like manner, often indexed perceptually by a reduced inversion effect for sexualized women relative to men.
criteria.X: Human cognition is capacity-limited, requiring strategies to actively structure information. Eye movements offer a natural mechanism for sequential sampling, but whether such sequences reflect memory organization is unknown.
criteria.Y: This narrative review examines a research program in psychology of music developed over two decades in Latin American South, tracing how studies at the intersection of music psychology, developmental psychology, and the philosophy of mind articulated a postcognitivist account of musical experience.
criteria.Z: Many models of cognition have sampling as a central component. Researchers have used them to explain human performance across a wide range of tasks involving perception, probability reasoning, and choice.
criteria.AA: A primary goal of systems neuroscience is to discover how ensembles of neurons transform inputs into goal-directed behavior, a process known as neural computation.
criteria.AB: Fear discrimination—the ability to distinguish threatening stimuli from non-threatening ones—is an essential adaptive behavior, yet the neural mechanisms underlying individual differences in discrimination precision remain unclear.
criteria.AC: The relative contributions of spectral and temporal cues to voice pitch perception in cochlear implant (CI) users remain unclear. This study aimed to directly quantify these contributions in dynamic speech stimuli with clinical n-of-m processors.
criteria.AD: Depression is a common mental disorder that seriously affects mental health and quality of life. Traditional depression diagnosis mainly relies on clinical interviews and subjective assessments, which may lead to variability in diagnostic outcomes.
criteria.AE: Understanding how facial characteristics associated with intellectual disability are processed during early stages of perception may provide new insights into disability-related social cognition.
criteria.AF: Early detection of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is essential for timely clinical intervention, yet remains challenging due to subtle neural changes in its initial stages.

criteria.AC: Total antioxidant capacity (TAC) reflects the collective ability of biological systems to counteract oxidative stress and is therefore an important indicator in redox biology, nutritional evaluation, and clinical assessment.

questions.instructions:
Here is the title of a recently published study: Teachers’ perceptions and self-reported practices regarding teaching personal and social skills in primary physical education: A survey study

Below are 32 candidates, each the start of a published abstract from the same research area. Which candidate starts the abstract of this study?

criteria.A: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is frequently associated with postural instability, including camptocormia, an involuntary anterior flexion of the thoracolumbar spine.
criteria.B: Although motor and cognitive functions are closely interconnected in daily life, they are typically assessed separately in fall assessments.
criteria.C: Personalized feedback can support motor learning while also increasing reliance on external guidance.
criteria.D: The global increase in the aging population has led to a rise in age-related functional decline, particularly in institutional care settings in low- and middle-income countries.
criteria.E: Physical literacy, originally developed within physical education settings to foster lasting engagement in physical activity, is increasingly recognized in Canada as a multidimensional framework encompassing physical, cognitive, and affective dimensions that support health and participation.
criteria.F: Physical education is often criticized for relying on repetitive sport-based activities while neglecting broader educational aims such as personal development, conflict resolution, and sustainability.
criteria.G: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) is a common complication of diabetes mellitus that may impair balance, mobility, and functional independence. Exercise using unstable surfaces, such as Wobble Board and Swiss Ball, may improve these functional outcomes.
criteria.H: Many patients have been treated by physical therapists after an infection with COVID-19. The policy changes and unique situation of the COVID-19 pandemic necessitate a retrospective analysis.
criteria.I: This study aimed to establish scientific criteria and identify an appropriate battery of specific physical fitness tests with adequate reliability and validity for Vietnamese university students enrolled in elective basketball courses.
criteria.J: Wearable inertial sensors have become tools for objectively assessing mobility in older people. This study analyzed whether wearable inertial sensors could detect exercise-induced mobility changes and compared the effects of multicomponent training (MCT) and elastic band training (EBT) on mobility and physical function in older women.
criteria.K: Physical education provides an important context for adolescents’ social development because students regularly interact with teachers and peers through cooperation, competition, and shared learning experiences.
criteria.L: Parkinson’s disease requires continuous assessment and long-term rehabilitation; however, access to in-person care is often limited by mobility constraints and healthcare availability.
criteria.M: Personal and social development constitutes an important goal of physical education (PE) curricula worldwide.
criteria.N: Freezing of gait (FOG) is a debilitating symptom in Parkinson’s disease (PD), characterized by paroxysmal episodes wherein there is an inability to step effectively, despite attempting to do so.
criteria.O: Existing prediction models may not sufficiently account for sex-specific contribution patterns and often lack interpretability. This study applied a sex-stratified, multi-model machine learning approach with SHAP-based interpretability to predict one-year fall incidence and characterize sex differences in feature contribution patterns.
criteria.P: This paper explores the process of cross-border collaboration among physical education teacher educators and pre-service teachers from the North and South of Ireland, jurisdictions that share a politically significant border.
criteria.Q: Quadriceps function contributes to lower-extremity support during single-limb tasks. It can be characterized by maximal voluntary contraction (MVC) and submaximal torque steadiness.
criteria.R: Gender perspective (GP) has gained increasing legitimacy in initial teacher education, although challenges remain regarding its translation into conceptually grounded practices.
criteria.S: Previous research on sexual diversity in physical education (PE) has predominantly addressed LGB (lesbian, gay, bisexual) teachers and students who conceal their sexual orientation within school contexts.
criteria.T: Frailty is defined as a prevalent geriatric syndrome characterized by reduced physiological reserve and heightened susceptibility to stress.
criteria.U: This article gave recommendations on the development of strength abilities of student girls in hand nosology and studied their anthropometric and functional indicators.
criteria.V: This study compared health-related physical fitness levels among Semester 3 pre-university Sports Science students at SMK Khir Johari using the Prudential FITNESSGRAM test battery.
criteria.W: Physical contact is frequently used in sports instruction, but perceptions of discomfort may vary according to social and contextual factors.
criteria.X: The evolving demands of physical education in contemporary school contexts require future teachers to be equipped with pedagogical approaches that are responsive, adaptable, and grounded in the realities of dynamic learning environments.
criteria.Y: The Work Disability Functional Assessment Battery (WD-FAB) was developed based on the International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) framework and administered using a computer adaptive test (CAT) to assess individuals' functional status.
criteria.Z: Although cycling offers numerous health benefits, age-related functional decline can increase the risk of accidents. Identifying balance components linked to outdoor cycling competence could inform targeted assessment and training.
criteria.AA: Orienteering is an endurance-running sport that combines physical activity with cognitive demands. The main goal is to complete a predefined route, navigating through specific control points with the help of a map and a compass.
criteria.AB: Italy’s Law 234/2021 introduced specialist physical education (PE) teachers into grades 4–5 of primary school (ages 9–11), replacing exclusively generalist provision for the subject.
criteria.AC: The Timed Up and Go (TUG) test is widely used to assess mobility and fall risk in older adults, but total completion time does not capture phase-specific motor control.
criteria.AD: Drug-induced parkinsonism is a potentially reversible movement disorder that may be subtle and difficult to monitor in residential dementia care. Vision-based machine learning analysis of gait may provide unobtrusive longitudinal monitoring around medication changes.
criteria.AE: Gait impairment, postural instability, and freezing of gait are major contributors to mobility limitations in Parkinson’s disease (PD). Robot-assisted gait training (RAGT) has emerged as a promising rehabilitation strategy; however, its association with phase-specific lower-limb kinetic outcomes remains insufficiently characterized.
criteria.AF: RESEARCH PURPOSE: Based on Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study systematically examines the effectiveness of Physical Education Teacher Education (PETE) curriculum from the perspective of student satisfaction.

questions.instructions:
Find the abstract that matches a title.

Title: Perceived quality of nursing education from a health systems perspective: a cross-sectional study of two universities in Albania

All options are opening lines of abstracts from the field of Research and Theory. Which option opens the abstract of the work with the title above?

criteria.A: This study aimed to examine the factors related to the visiting nurse staff's intention to continue working and to obtain nursing management implications for their continued employment.
criteria.B: Missed nursing care threatens quality and safety, but patient counts may not capture shift-level demands. We examined associations of patient-count and perceived workload indicators with missed care, separating within- and between-nurse effects.
criteria.C: Job frustration among mental health nurses can have determinant impact on staff wellbeing, retention, and quality of care. However, little is known about the factors contributing to job frustration and the coping strategies used by mental health nurses in Oman.
criteria.D: The global shortage of nurses places additional pressure on healthcare systems and nursing education. Effective mentoring is crucial for students, and various interventions have been developed to enhance the mentoring competences of nurses working with undergraduate nursing students.
criteria.E: Unfinished Nursing Care (UNC) in Neonatal Intensive Care Units (NICUs) is a critical determinant of infant outcomes. The Neonatal Extent of Work Rationing Instrument (NEWRI) measures the frequency of UNC but not the underlying reasons.
criteria.F: Students’ satisfaction is a key indicator of the effectiveness and quality of nursing education, reflecting how well institutions address academic, clinical, and professional needs.
criteria.G: Nurses are the backbone of healthcare systems, and their retention remains a critical global challenge, as high attrition leads to a loss of expertise, continuity of care, and patient trust.
criteria.H: Modern healthcare systems operate in an environment characterized by rapid technological development, increasing patient expectations, and growing complexity of medical services.
criteria.I: Career plateauing is an increasingly recognized workforce challenge in nursing, associated with reduced motivation, professional growth, and retention.
criteria.J: Nutritional care is a fundamental aspect of nursing influencing patients’ health outcomes. Recognised as a human right and a basic need, nutritional care underscores the importance of integrating it into nursing education programmes.
criteria.K: Strategic communication plays a vital role in healthcare organizations undergoing continuous cultural transformation, yet its impact on reinforcing nurses' professional identity remains underexplored.
criteria.L: Professional development is essential for nurses to maintain skills, deliver quality care, and adapt to healthcare changes. In Bangladesh, nurses often face barriers to continuing professional development (CPD), affecting career growth and service quality.
criteria.M: To adapt the Individual Workload Perception Scale-Revised (IWPS-R) into Spanish and evaluate its psychometric properties among nursing professionals. Methods: We performed a cross-cultural adaptation following Beaton's protocol, including translation, back-translation, and expert committee review.
criteria.N: Effective leadership especially shared leadership is essential-forimproving nursing staff team performance, particularly in critical careenvironments like Intensive Care–Unit (ICU).
criteria.O: Nurses are experiencing various negative consequences as a resultof a toxic environment caused by despotic leadership. Nursing managers need todo away such leadership in order to enhance nurses' well-being and workplacethat strengthen group cohesiveness and create a psychologically secure free fromemotional dissonance.
criteria.P: Curriculum development for nursing education in medical technical schools serves as a critical foundation for preparing competent nursing professionals who meet the evolving demands of modern healthcare systems.
criteria.Q: Missed nursing care (MNC) refers to the omission or delay of care resulting from systemic problems, which is particularly dangerous in oncology and places a burden on patients and nurses.
criteria.R: Continuing Nursing Education (CNE) is an essential aspect of lifelong learning that helps nurses improve their knowledge, clinical skills, and professional competence for quality patient care.
criteria.S: Organizational silence, referring to employees' reluctance to voice their opinions and constructive suggestions, can have an adverse impact on hospitals, individuals, and patient safety.
criteria.T: Quality improvement is a global healthcare priority. In Ghana, consistent delivery of high-quality nursing care remains challenging, and the perspectives of nurses and nurse managers are often underrepresented in discussions on care quality.
criteria.U: Nursing students’ perceptions of educational quality – particularly the clinical learning environment (CLE) – are an early indicator of whether programs are producing graduates who feel ready for practice.
criteria.V: Healthcare systems face increasing complexity alongside persistent nursing shortages. Shared Governance, operationalized through Unit Practice Councils, is a professional practice model designed to strengthen nurse engagement, accountability and evidence‑informed decision-making at the point of care.
criteria.W: Sustaining mental health capability in undergraduate nursing education requires an academic workforce able to teach, interpret and steward that knowledge over time.
criteria.X: Postgraduate leadership education is increasingly recognised as essential for preparing nurses to navigate the complexities of contemporary healthcare.
criteria.Y: Leadership and management competencies are critical in health care to ensure quality service delivery, yet they are often underemphasized in traditional nursing education.
criteria.Z: A supportive practice environment is essential for nurse retention and to enable nurses to provide effective person-centred care. When nurses are prevented from acting according to their professional values, they may experience moral distress, potentially leading to disengagement and increased turnover intention.
criteria.AA: Nurse turnover remains a major challenge for health systems, yet objective, scalable measures of workload that predict turnover are limited. Electronic health record (EHR) audit logs offer a potential data source to quantify nursing work patterns.
criteria.AB: This qualitative descriptive phenomenological study explores the lived experiences and professional challenges of 15 Job Order (JO) nurses at a public hospital in Bulacan during the academic year 2025–2026.
criteria.AC: This qualitative phenomenological study explored leadership role practices and their influence on nurses' professional development in a private tertiary hospital in Marikina City.
criteria.AD: Job satisfaction among nursing staff is a key determinant of workforce stability, quality of care, and healthcare system sustainability. Nurses are increasingly exposed to high workload, staffing shortages, and complex organizational demands, which may adversely affect satisfaction and retention.
criteria.AE: Role ambiguity undermines effective professional governance in nursing, particularly in complex, rapidly evolving health care systems where decision-making authority is distributed.
criteria.AF: Monitoring vital signs (VS) is a key nursing responsibility for early detection of clinical deterioration and ensuring patient safety. Although VS measurements—such as body temperature, pulse, respiratory rate, and blood pressure—are simple, they are essential indicators.

questions.instructions:
You are matching papers to their abstracts. The paper is called: A prefrontal–bed nucleus pathway controls aversive memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids

Choose the option that is the first part of this paper's abstract (every option is from a paper in Cognitive Neuroscience).

criteria.A: The article is devoted to the psychological and pedagogical characteristics of left- handed children and ways of individualizing the educational process.
criteria.B: Adaptive memory requires balancing generalization to avoid similar threats with discrimination to recognize safety. criteria.C: The dentate (lateral) nucleus (DN) of the cerebellum is one of the major sources of afferent input to the ventrolateral (VL) thalamus, and further to the motor cortex.
criteria.D: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is increasingly characterized as a disorder of brain dynamics, but the temporal scale on which resting-state activity differs from healthy controls remains unclear.

criteria.G: We present an active inference account of persistent dizziness predicated on models of enactivism and ecological psychology; including first-hand accounts of the patient’s lived experience.
criteria.H: Operant conditioning is a powerful method for probing cognitive functions, yet its widespread use is constrained by low throughput, labor-intensive procedures, and high costs.
criteria.I: Working memory involves complex activity and interactions across multiple brain areas. However, little is known about how these large-scale activity and interaction patterns relate to resting-state activity and to excitatory and inhibitory interactions within localized brain regions.

criteria.K: Electroencephalogram (EEG) signal classification plays a pivotal role in brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) and the diagnosis of neurological disorders.
criteria.L: The use of electroencephalography (EEG) in automated screening of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) has created a large body of literature that suggests promising outcomes, with reported classification accuracies often above 90%.
criteria.M: Prior work has shown that memory typically gets worse over time, and narrative memory is better the more causally connected an event is within the story.

criteria.O: Language and vision are two primary source modalities of information for humans. To uncover shared and unique mental representations across linguistic and visual inputs, one approach is to test the extent to which a certain neural signature is shared.
criteria.P: Typical visual displays cover only a fraction of the visual field. How do such restrictions influence the perception of visual speed during self-motion?
criteria.Q: Understanding mixed emotions is crucial for capturing the ambivalence of human information processing. However, how specific visual factors, such as outward appearance and motion, interact to evoke these conflicting feelings remains unclear.
criteria.R: Within the general population, approximately 6% of people will have posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and 15% will have depression at one point in their life, yet little is known about how symptoms of PTSD and depression affect people’s ability to accurately report details of a witnessed traumatic event.
criteria.S: In a delayed alternation spatial working memory task, hippocampal time cells fire during specific moments of the delay period to form a sequential representation of the entire delay interval.
criteria.T: Visual memory is known to be influenced by objective image properties, including image size and contrast, as well as visual category. However, the influence of illusory perceptual experience on memory remains less understood.

criteria.X: Browser-based hearing tests offer a scalable alternative to clinic-based assessment, but most validated tools have been developed in English-speaking populations.

criteria.AC: Dopamine and norepinephrine regulate hippocampal plasticity through molecular, cellular and circuit mechanisms that shape which experiences are encoded and later remembered.
criteria.AD: The prefrontal cortex (PFC) is implicated in many cognitive tasks, including working memory, reward-based decision-making, executive control, and metacognition.
criteria.AE: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with cognitive dysfunction and emotional disturbances, in which the hippocampus and amygdala are key limbic structures.
criteria.AF: The relative contributions of spectral and temporal cues to voice pitch perception in cochlear implant (CI) users remain unclear. This study aimed to directly quantify these contributions in dynamic speech stimuli with clinical n-of-m processors.

Title of a research article: Resource-Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Edge System for Wind Turbine Blade Defect Diagnosis

Each option below is the beginning of the abstract of an article from the same subject area (Civil and Structural Engineering). Which option is the beginning of this article's abstract?

criteria.A: Roman aqueduct bridges are widespread across the seismically active Mediterranean, yet their earthquake vulnerability remains insufficiently documented.
criteria.B: Accurate fatigue damage estimation is a critical step for managing and extending the life of wind turbine fleets, and the basis on which operators decide whether an ageing asset can be kept in service beyond the end of design life.

criteria.D: Road tunnels are indispensable components of transport networks, providing critical connections while operating continuously under demanding environmental, geological, and hydrogeological conditions.
criteria.E: For bridges in long-term operation, only limited abnormal samples with clear labels are available, which makes it difficult to apply conventional supervised methods that require sufficient labeled data.
criteria.F: Mechanically stabilized earth (MSE) construction presents a viable approach for the effective utilization of space, particularly in the design and stabilization of slopes and embankments.

criteria.C: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) and ocean acidity extremes (OAXs) are intensifying under anthropogenic climate change, and their compound co-occurrence can amplify ecological impacts.
criteria.D: Acoustic Doppler Current Profilers (ADCPs) are widely deployed to characterise tidal currents in energetic marine environments. While instruments and deployment techniques have improved reliability, data usability remains constrained by workflow, metadata, and archival practices.
criteria.E: Epiphytic algae threaten the productivity of cultivated carrageenophytes, particularly Kappaphycus spp. and Eucheuma denticulatum, yet their diversity remains poorly documented.
criteria.F: Chlorophyll ‐a (Chl ‐a ) is the most widely used proxy for phytoplankton biomass, bloom intensity, and trophic status in marine ecosystems.
criteria.G: This study establishes a numerical wave simulation framework based on Simulating Waves Nearshore (SWAN) to investigate the characteristics of typhoon-generated waves in the coastal waters of the northern South China Sea.
criteria.H: Sea Surface Salinity (SSS) trends and variability have been studied for long periods of time, using historical archives and Argo float data.
criteria.I: At higher latitudes there are many land-locked fjords with shallow threshold sills or channels and deep basins inside. The renewal of water within these deep, semi-enclosed, basins is essential to maintaining water quality (e.g. dissolved oxygen levels), particularly at depth.
criteria.J: Understanding the composition and spatial pattern of deep-sea benthic habitats is important for marine conservation. However, biological observations remain sparse in deep-sea regions, and broad-scale habitat classifications still rely largely on environmental variables as surrogates for benthic organisms.
criteria.K: Seaweed aquaculture production is expanding globally but threatened by increasing climate stressors, including extreme events. Ocean-based aquaculture is especially vulnerable to marine heatwaves, which can rapidly raise temperatures above the physiological limits of organisms, including macroalgae.
criteria.L: Studies on the effects of long-term climate change on marine communities are crucial to our understanding of ecosystem resilience. The Late Quaternary fossil record, dominated by extant taxa, provides a valuable archive of past biotic responses to major climate fluctuations.
criteria.M: Seagrass restoration increasingly relies on seed-based approaches, yet optimal seeding densities and deployment methods remain poorly resolved. We evaluated the relative effects of seed density and clam-mediated seed placement on eelgrass ( Zostera marina ) establishment in a field restoration experiment in Back Sound, North Carolina.
criteria.N: In the Arctic, where the effects of the changing climate are occurring faster than anywhere else on Earth, warming, sea-ice decline, and changes in ocean circulation have resulted in increased marine primary productivity.
criteria.O: Groundwater resources in Jharkhand, India, are under increasing stress due to escalating demand from urban, peri-urban, and agricultural sectors, requiring improved spatial characterisation of groundwater dynamics.
criteria.P: Understanding marine organismal responses to co-occurring climate stressors is critical for predicting changes in ecosystems and commercial fisheries.
criteria.Q: Acceleration, rather than a gradual linear response, is emerging as a defining feature of ocean change in the Anthropocene. Surface‐forced warming propagates into the deep ocean over decades to centuries, but semi‐enclosed basins such as the Mediterranean Sea may respond more rapidly.
criteria.R: Lake St Lucia forms part of the iSimangaliso Wetland Park, South Africa’s first UNESCO World Heritage Site. Freshwater deprivation over multiple decades and a closed mouth condition in Lake St Lucia led to the loss of ecosystem functioning and marine connectivity, with cascading negative effects on ecotourism and other stakeholders in the region.
criteria.S: Storm Louis struck south-western Europe between 22 and 26 February 2024, producing severe metocean conditions that led to significant disruptions in transportation networks, widespread power outages and one confirmed fatality.
criteria.T: Satellite observations can extend benthic biodiversity monitoring beyond sparse point surveys, but their value depends on robust field validation and transparent uncertainty.
criteria.U: Accurate prediction of tidal current velocities is crucial for various applications, such as estimating energy production in tidal power projects. However, Acoustic Doppler current profiler (ADCP) campaigns are often expensive and can lead to incomplete data.
criteria.V: Marine heatwaves (MHWs) are prolonged anomalies of warm sea surface temperature (SST) that can disrupt marine ecosystems, physical climate processes, and human coastal activities.
criteria.W: Diatoms are the dominant primary producers south of the Antarctic Polar Front (~60°S) and play a central role in Southern Ocean food webs and the biological carbon pump.
criteria.X: The Labrador Sea is a key region for carbon dioxide uptake characterized by deep mixing during winter that supplies nutrients to the upper water column and fuels extensive phytoplankton blooms in spring.
criteria.Y: Accurate prediction of ocean surface currents is essential for maritime safety in narrow waterways with strong tidal forcing. This study presents a three-phase evaluation of forecasting methods for high-frequency (HF) radar surface currents in the Sunda Strait, Indonesia, where tidal currents regularly exceed 150 cm s −1 .
criteria.Z: Chlorophyll-a concentration is known to influence the mean-state and interannual sea surface temperature (SST) variability of the tropics. Here, we investigate this effect in the equatorial Atlantic Ocean using a suite of ocean model simulations.
criteria.AA: Fungi are frequently recorded in marine environments worldwide, commonly associated with inert or living substrates in shallow temperate waters as well as in deep, cold and dark habitats.
criteria.AB: The European Macaronesian region (Azores, Madeira, Canary Islands) represents a key biogeographic transition zone in the Northeast Atlantic. While its large-scale gradients are well recognized, the extent to which long-term variability and vertical structure shape ecosystem dynamics remains poorly quantified.
criteria.AC: In recent years, more frequent marine heatwaves (MHWs) in the South China Sea (SCS) have affected surface chlorophyll-a (Chl-a). Traditional linear statistical methods have limited capacity to identify the contributions of multiple highly interrelated physical drivers in complex oceanic systems.
criteria.AD: Bottom friction coefficients (BFCs) are critical parameters in tidal modeling, with significant effects on hydrodynamic conditions and sediment transport.
criteria.AE: The population of Bolboschoenoplectus mariqueter has substantially declined because of habitat modification and competition. Therefore, this study aimed to characterize the photosynthetic and stoichiometric traits of B. mariqueter and their environmental regulation in a natural tidal-flat population to facilitate successful conservation.
criteria.AF: Harmful algal blooms of Alexandrium monilatum and Margalefidinium polykrikoides are a common occurrence in the tributaries of lower Chesapeake Bay, United States of America.

questions.instructions:
Title of a research article: Towards a structural analysis of interesting geometric theorems: analysis of a survey

Each option below is the beginning of the abstract of an article from the same subject area (Geometry and Topology). Which option is the beginning of this article's abstract?

criteria.A: In this paper, we establish several new deterministic and random fixed point theorems for applications satisfying some condition via concept of degree of nondensifiability (DND for short).
criteria.B: We develop a unified discrete framework for computing and analyzing degree-based topological indices of Cartesian graph products, a class of constructions that plays a central role in applied and structural graph theory.
criteria.C: Partamona helleri is a stingless bee distributed across the Atlantic Forest, one of Brazil's most threatened biomes. We analyzed wing size and shape in 26 populations spanning the species' latitudinal range to evaluate their associations with environmental variables.
criteria.D: The association between craniofacial morphology and the cross-sectional areas (CSA) of the masseter and medial pterygoid muscles using Procrustes-based geometric morphometrics on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data was investigated.
criteria.E: In this manuscript, we investigate original fixed-point (fp) and fixed-disc results in quasi M-metric spaces. First, we present a Hardy–Rogers-type fp result for self-mappings satisfying a specific contractive condition in mq-complete quasi M-metric spaces.
criteria.F: Symmetry is a fundamental property of biological systems, yet it is commonly reduced to discrete, subjective classifications that fail to capture the continuous and graded nature of symmetry in real organisms.
criteria.G: We give a formula with explicit constants relating the subsurface projection of the end invariants of a hyperbolic 3‐manifold diffeomorphic to and the length of the geodesic representative in of the multicurve .
criteria.H: Fluctuating asymmetry (FA) is commonly used as a phenotypic indicator related to developmental stability, reflecting variation in an organism’s ability to maintain bilateral correspondence during development.
criteria.I: In this paper, we investigate the existence of coincidence points for g-interpolative Kannan and g-interpolative Ćirić–Reich–Rus contraction mappings in the framework of rectangular m-metric spaces.
criteria.J: We construct an explicit example of an asymptotically conformal chord-arc curve that fails to be asymptotically smooth.
criteria.K: The binding affinity between an antibody and an antigen, measured by the equilibrium dissociation constant ( K d ) and the associated Gibbs free energy of binding ( Δ G ) , is key to immune recognition and the design of therapeutic antibodies.
criteria.L: I study central configurations in the four-body problem, i.e., configurations in which the forces on all the bodies point to a fixed, single point in space.
criteria.M: Morphological modularity is known to favour evolutionary diversification by enabling different body regions to vary in response to functional and ecological demands.
criteria.N: The potential of shape variation to distinguish between species can be examined using quantitative approaches such as 2D or 3D geometric morphometrics (GM).
criteria.O: This paper presents a systematic survey of bifurcation theory for near-Hamiltonian systems with finite-order smoothness.
criteria.P: Molecular graph theory has been widely used to represent the structure of chemical compounds and to study their physicochemical properties. In this work, we introduce a set of stress sum-based indices and examine their usefulness in describing the structural characteristics of drugs used in Hodgkin lymphoma treatment.
criteria.Q: We study surgery descriptions of orientation-reversing periodic diffeomorphisms of compact orientable 3-manifolds in terms of standard symmetries of model manifolds.
criteria.R: Here, we discussed some relations between G-nonexpansive mappings and G−quasinonexpansive mappings and their structures. Further we obtained some convergence results of a sequence, defined by Schaefer iteration scheme for multi-valued Osilike-Berinde G-nonexpansive mapping in uniformly convex hyperbolic metric space.
criteria.S: Polynomial invariants are important tools for studying virtual knots, and different constructions encode different aspects of the combinatorial and geometric information of a virtual knot diagram.
criteria.T: The closest-point problem for a circular helix reduces to Kepler’s equation u+esinu=M with geometric eccentricity e=aρ/b2 unrestricted above. Building on this known reduction and earlier half-turn localization, we derive an exact stationary-point count and a theorem selecting the global minimizer.
criteria.U: In this paper, we introduce and investigate a normalized fractional Bessel–Maitland function generated through the Riemann–Liouville fractional derivative, thereby establishing a new connection between fractional calculus and geometric function theory.
criteria.V: A graph is called H-free if the graph has no subgraph being isomorphic to H. The classical Turán problem aims to determine the maximum size of an H-free graph with given order.
criteria.W: Spectral graph theory and group theory help reveal how the structure of graphs shapes their mathematical properties. This research aims to analyze the spectral descriptors of the prime coprime graph of a dihedral group associated with the Laplacian, normalized Laplacian, and Seidel matrices.
criteria.X: Cranial diversity within indigenous horse populations remains incompletely characterized. Cranial shape variation and its associations with skull size and sex were investigated in 37 adult Kyrgyz horses aged 4–5 years (18 females and 19 males).
criteria.Y: The sella turcica, a small depression within the sphenoid bone in mammal skulls, exhibits notable morphological variation across primates, including the occasional presence of accessory openings.
criteria.Z: This paper investigates codimension-one transverse bifurcations of simple robust homoclinic cycles with a pair of complex transverse eigenvalues in Γ-equivariant systems on R5.
criteria.AA: This study examines regional and genetic influences on shell morphology of the small giant clam Tridacna maxima from the central and northern Red Sea of Saudi Arabia using linear mixed model and geometric morphometrics.
criteria.AB: Unlike linear vector fields, which exhibit simple dynamics, piecewise linear vector fields support significantly richer and more complex behavior. For instance, whereas planar linear vector fields are known to be devoid of limit cycles, their piecewise counterparts may exhibit limit cycles.
criteria.AC: Subclasses of bi-univalent functions defined by the modified Tremblay operator and the Horadam polynomial generating function are investigated. Motivated by recent developments in geometric function theory, two subclasses are introduced through suitable subordination conditions involving the modified Tremblay operator.
criteria.AD: A longstanding challenge in automated theorem generation is not merely to derive new statements, but to identify which of them are mathematically interesting.
criteria.AE: Wings play a central role in shaping dispersal, behavior, and ecological specialization of insects. In social insects, distinct castes with specialized morphologies arise from a shared genome, raising the question of how divergence of traits, such as wings, occurs despite genetic constraints.
criteria.AF: In this work, we focus on the study of the components of semilevel sets of pseudoperiodic functions. Specifically, we provide partial proofs of a conjecture proposed by V.I.

questions.instructions:
Here is the title of a recently published study: From Flood Exposure to Adaptation Constraints: An RBQ-based Assessment of Flood-affected Farm Households in the North Bank Plains Zone of Assam, India

Below are 32 candidates, each the start of a published abstract from the same research area. Which candidate starts the abstract of this study?

criteria.A: Sesame ( Sesamum indicum L.) exhibits a mixed mating system, in which both self‐ and cross‐pollination can occur. In tropical environments, the contribution of pollinators may enhance fertilization efficiency and increase crop yield.
criteria.B: Six new species of the cleptoparasitic nomadine genus Kelita Sandhouse, 1943 are described from Chile, north of the Tropic of Capricorn, an area where no species of the genus were previously known.
criteria.C: An updated account of the treehoppers (Hemiptera: Membracidae) of Singapore is presented here. The addition of 16 new records increases the known fauna to 52 species (inclusive of 8 morphospecies) distributed across 11 tribes and 17 genera.
criteria.D: Reproduction is an important but costly life history stage, and birds may share this cooperatively through biparental care. However, parental efforts are not always shared equally, with many bird species exhibiting asymmetrical biparental care.
criteria.E: Within the Palaearctic, the Anatolian and Iberian Peninsulas are established centers of diversity for the genus Merodon Meigen, 1803. However, recent research also highlights the Eastern Mediterranean and the Middle East as important regions.
criteria.F: Assessing climate change impacts on agriculture is essential for developing effective adaptation strategies, with crop simulation models providing valuable tools for evaluating future crop productivity.
criteria.G: This study assessed the socio-economic effects of climate variability and community-led adaptation along the southeastern coastal zone of Côte d’Ivoire, from Abidjan to Aboisso.
criteria.H: Climate variability may affect cereal production through changes in rainfall and temperature patterns. This study assessed the relationship between climate variability and cereal yields in the agricultural zone of Niono, Mali, during 2010–2019, focusing on rice, millet and sorghum.
criteria.I: The Texas High Plains, a vital agricultural region, faces ongoing challenges from water scarcity and climate variability. This study investigated the spatial and temporal trends in major crops and cropping systems, including upland cotton, maize, sorghum, and wheat, from 1968 to 2023.
criteria.J: Sexually deceptive orchids mimic female mating signals of their pollinators to achieve pollination. In Australia, multiple orchid genera exploit male thynnine wasps as pollinators, raising the possibility of convergent evolution of floral traits.
criteria.K: Insect pollinator declines are increasingly documented worldwide, yet assessment of pollination resilience often focuses on species loss or current ecosystem function without explicitly considering changes in interaction structure and recovery history.
criteria.L: Livestock sustainability research increasingly addresses ecological, institutional, cultural, economic, technological, and ethical problems, yet cross-site comparisons and benchmarking frameworks often leave underexamined the conditions under which findings, metrics, and interventions become comparable or transferable across production settings.
criteria.M: Integrated Farming System (IFS) is an important approach to improving resource-use efficiency, farm productivity, and sustainability through the integration of crop and allied enterprises.
criteria.N: The migratory locust, Locusta migratoria, exhibits density-dependent phase polyphenism. In June 2026, a large outbreak occurred on reclaimed agricultural land in Goheung, Republic of Korea.
criteria.O: Worldwide, the division of ancestral land has reduced the size of operational farm holdings. In Northeast India, 78.9% of smallholders cultivate micro-plots plagued by resource constraints and seasonal water shortages, rendering single-enterprise agriculture unsustainable.
criteria.P: To assess and compare farmers’ preferences for adaptation strategies to water scarcity in Chittur (Palakkad district, Kerala) and Pollachi North (Coimbatore district, Tamil Nadu), two groundwater-dependent farming regions on either side of the Palakkad Gap.
criteria.Q: This review is of the recently revised circumscriptions of the Pleurophyllum Hook.f. group and Shawia J.R.Forst. & G.Forst. of subtribe Celmisiinae, both centred in New Zealand.
criteria.R: Seventeen species of Tetrastichus Haliday from China are reviewed, including three country records species: T. brevicalcar Graham, 1991, T. pilemostomae Graham, 1991, T. temporalis (Graham) and new provincial distribution records are provided for another fourteen species.
criteria.S: Fungal diseases such as Alternaria leaf blight of sesame and collar rot of groundnut significantly limit the productivity of these important oilseed crops.
criteria.T: Recurrent flooding affects agricultural production in Assam’s North Bank Plain Zone, but the relative severity of farming constraints and barriers to climate-resilient adaptation requires closer examination.
criteria.U: Late spring frost is a major abiotic stress affecting winter wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) production, yet its impact on yield remains difficult to quantify because crop responses depend not only on the intensity of low‐temperature exposure but also on environmental conditions following frost events.
criteria.V: Uttarakhand has a predominantly rural population, with agriculture serving as a key livelihood for many people.
criteria.W: Understanding plant responses to both day and night heat is essential for developing climate smart agriculture systems to sustain global food production.
criteria.X: In China, Phortica okadai is the only established vector for Thelazia callipaeda and transmits infective larvae to various animals feeding on ocular secretions.
criteria.Y: Mussaenda wallichii G. Don (Rubiaceae) is a widespread species distributed from northeastern India to Southeast Asia, but its taxonomic delimitation has remained uncertain due to overlapping morphological characters and incomplete assessment of type materials.
criteria.Z: This study examined the effects of climate change on coffee yields of smallholder farmers and their adaptation strategies in Bunyangabu District, Uganda.
criteria.AA: Wild bees are declining worldwide, with urbanisation as one major driver. Urban environments can filter for wild bees with specific functional traits and resource requirements.
criteria.AB: Climate change poses an increasing threat to agricultural production and food security. While many European countries have developed National Adaptation Strategies (NASs) and National Adaptation Plans (NAPs), the alignment between proposed policies and their supporting mechanisms remains under-explored.
criteria.AC: Wild bees, main providers of vital pollination services to wild and crop plants, are in decline in many ecosystems.
criteria.AD: Climate change continues to increase the frequency and intensity of events, threatening agricultural production, farmers' livelihoods and the achievement of SDGs 1 and 2 (No Poverty and Zero Hunger).
criteria.AE: In this study, the potential and limitations of iNaturalist for monitoring mosses in Poland (2019–2025) were assessed using 17,451 verified “Research Grade” records.
criteria.AF: The global expansion of agriculture, particularly the cultivation of mass‐flowering crops and the introduction of industrial‐scale beekeeping, threatens biodiversity by disrupting plant–pollinator interactions in natural communities.

questions.instructions:
Find the abstract that matches a title.

Title: Doing, saying, and evaluating authority: transitivity patterns in Dayak Bentian women’s interaction

All options are opening lines of abstracts from the field of Language and Linguistics. Which option opens the abstract of the work with the title above?

criteria.A: While Foreign Language Enjoyment (FLE) has been widely investigated in English learning, Chinese as a Foreign Language Enjoyment (CFLE) remains underexplored, particularly in AI-supported culturally immersive contexts.
criteria.B: This article examines how English technology terms are semantically reconfigured in contemporary Uzbek online media.
criteria.C: As multilingual digital communication increasingly integrates linguistic, visual, and other semiotic resources, understanding how code-switching operates across multiple modes has become an important issue in contemporary sociolinguistic and discourse-analytic research.
criteria.D: As a genre of institutional talk, broadcast interviews require interviewers and interviewees to design their talk for an overhearing audience. Based on data from Indonesian broadcast interviews, this study explores the tension that arises between adhering to this institutional norm and simultaneously addressing one another.
criteria.E: Authеntic mеdical tеxts еxposе lеarnеrs to languagе usеd for rеal profеssional and public communication. Howеvеr, rеading an authеntic sourcе doеs not automatically dеvеlop thе ability to communicatе its contеnt.
criteria.F: This paper examines how nineteenth-century French and German scholars mobilised semantic plurality in thirty key texts focused on linguistic meaning.
criteria.G: In recent years, there has been a rapid increase in the use of technology to assist in the delivery of second language oral communication (OC) assessments.
criteria.H: A large and emerging body of evidence has challenged the classic view that L2 anxiety is a causal factor in L2 learning achievement and that when anxiety is mitigated, L2 proficiency improves.
criteria.I: Foreign language anxiety (FLA) has been identified as an essential topic in second language (L2) acquisition because affect strongly shapes students’ engagement with L2 learning.
criteria.J: This research aimed to investigate the effect of Interactive Learning Strategy on students’ reading comprehension at SMKN 2 Padang Panjang. The study was motivated by students’ difficulties in comprehending English texts due to the limited engagement associated with teacher-centered learning.
criteria.K: As Generative AI (GenAI) expands voice interaction capabilities, it offers new possibilities for foreign language speaking practice in more realistic interactional environments.
criteria.L: This cross‐sectional quantitative study focuses on the effect of practices in the educational context such as streaming on the relationships between foreign language learner emotions and proficiency.
criteria.M: Despite growing interest in growth mindset within second language acquisition (SLA) research, mindset interventions have produced consistently modest and context-dependent effects, suggesting that the construct may be theoretically mispositioned.
criteria.N: Input-based theories of second language acquisition (SLA) and Vygotskian sociocultural theory (SCT) explain similar phenomena using different conceptual frameworks.
criteria.O: This article examines the pedagogical role of authentic materials in English language teaching. Authentic materials include texts, recordings, videos, and everyday documents that were created for real communication rather than for classroom instruction.
criteria.P: This study investigated whether color-based signaling of argumentative elements (e.g., claims , counterclaims ) affects teacher judgment accuracy and assessment bias.
criteria.Q: Conversations involving potentially sensitive topics across cultures pose challenges not only for L2 speakers engaged in intercultural communication but also for researchers seeking to understand the mechanisms of such interactions.
criteria.R: Who decides what counts as “correct” or standard language today? Correcting language has always been an act of authority.
criteria.S: Building on a preliminary quantitative study that identified the dominance of positive emotions over negative emotions in EFL listening classes, this study extends that inquiry to explain these patterns qualitatively and examine their relationship with learner engagement in EFL listening instruction.
criteria.T: This article examines the structural organization of contemporary English financial-economic terminology, with particular attention to simple terms, derived terms, compounds, and multi-word terminological units.
criteria.U: In translated language research, Lithuanian is still an underrepresented language, although there are several parallel and comparable corpora which could be used as data sources in corpus-based translation studies.
criteria.V: This scoping review examined motivational regulation strategies (MRSs) in English as a foreign language (EFL) learning, focusing on the available literature, measurement instruments, antecedents, and effects.
criteria.W: In this paper, we propose a fine-grained, empirically-driven formalisation of framing in discourse, with a particular focus on dialogical interaction.
criteria.X: The aim of this article was to identify the patterns of interrelation between syntactic form and lexical semantics in the Ancient Greek text “The Life of Antony the Great” as a means of constructing a religious narrative.
criteria.Y: This article examines the morphological structure and word-formation patterns of fisheries-related terminology in the English language.
criteria.Z: Although pedagogical translanguaging has gained increasing attention in multilingual education, little is known about how learners perceive teacher-provided translanguaging written corrective feedback (WCF) compared with conventional English-only WCF.
criteria.AA: Language assessment rubrics sometimes ask raters to judge learners’ willingness and involvement alongside language and content quality. However, it is unclear whether these ratings capture distinct learner characteristics or simply reflect overall performance quality.
criteria.AB: The role of metalinguistic knowledge in transfer patterns in L3 is unclear. Although several recent studies have provided data on learners’ transfer patterns from L1 versus L2 in L3 French, these largely come from off-line tasks which may rely on metalinguistic knowledge.
criteria.AC: The article substantiates the role of foreign language teachers’ empathy as a leading factor in creating a psychologically safe learning environment that helps learners overcome the language barrier.
criteria.AD: This article examines the pedagogical conditions for establishing an integrative approach to developing students' didactic competence in English language teacher education at pedagogical universities in Uzbekistan.
criteria.AE: Whether a foreign language is experienced as difficult is less an objective property of the language system than a subjective belief, linked to language attitudes and to beliefs about one's own capacity to cope, that may influence motivation and learning behavior.
criteria.AF: This study examines how transitivity configurations contribute to authority-related meanings in Dayak Bentian women’s interaction. Drawing on approximately three hours of naturally occurring talk in domestic and communal settings, the study employs qualitative clause-level analysis informed by Systemic Functional Linguistics.

questions.instructions:
A journal article is titled "Comparative Assessment of Electric Vehicle Charging Impacts on the IEEE 33-Bus and Ayepe 34-Bus Distribution Networks".

Only one of the following abstract openings comes from that article; the others come from other recent articles in Electrical and Electronic Engineering. Which one is it?

criteria.A: This review critically discusses the development of continuous monitoring biosensors and the technological developments that have facilitated the transition from one-off or periodic measurement sensors to longer-term, connected and autonomous sensors.
criteria.B: The growing demand for safer and longer-lasting lithium-ion batteries has highlighted the limitations of conventional liquid electrolytes, particularly their susceptibility to oxidative decomposition and interfacial degradation.
criteria.C: High photovoltaic (PV) penetration can produce voltage rise, reverse power flow, feeder congestion, and less effective use of battery energy storage in radial distribution networks.
criteria.D: Capturing the cross-layer kinetics of intercalants remains a fundamental bottleneck in understanding the structural evolution of layered host materials.
criteria.E: Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE)-based trilateration is attractive for indoor positioning because it can operate with low-cost infrastructure, yet RSSI-derived distances can become geometrically incompatible in real deployments.
criteria.F: The lithographic performance of chemically amplified resists is strongly influenced by the balance among the functional components of the resist polymer.
criteria.G: Planning fast-charging infrastructure for electric vehicles (EVs) supports sustainable transport electrification. This study identifies when a corridor-wide plan along Puerto Rico Highway 2 (PR-2) becomes infeasible and which modeled constraint limits it first.
criteria.H: Laser self-mixing interference (SMI) with dual external-cavity optical feedback exhibits a distinct characteristic: a change in the length of one external cavity periodically modulates the amplitude of the SMI signal produced by the other external cavity.
criteria.I: With the rapid development of renewable energy, the large-scale integration of distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation into urban distribution networks has resulted in increasingly complex topologies and frequent PV power fluctuations, posing challenges for fault-state assessment and time-constrained restoration decision-making.
criteria.J: Hydrogen energy plants, comprising of water electrolyzers, fuel cells, compressors, storage systems, and associated Balance of Plant components, represent a central pillar of the emerging green energy transition.
criteria.K: This paper presents a rigorous comparison of two three-phase, five-level inverters intended to supply a squirrel-cage induction machine.
