criteria.L: Thermal evaporation of perovskite films holds considerable promise for the scalable manufacturing and pixel patterning of perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs).
criteria.M: Coordinating capacity configuration and operational scheduling in multi-energy systems is inherently complex, given their distinct time scales and intertwined economic and carbon constraints.
criteria.N: The increasing adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) introduces additional demand into existing distribution networks, potentially increasing power losses and weakening voltage stability.
criteria.O: The use of localized high‐concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) has emerged as a promising strategy to improve the stability of Li metal electrodes while overcoming the high viscosity and cost associated with high‐concentration electrolytes (HCEs).
criteria.P: The growing sophistication and need to have sustainable energy systems has led to the shift of the conventional power grids to smart power grids.
criteria.Q: The growing deployment of electric vehicles (EVs) and renewable energy sources (RES) brings about a substantial variability in demand and generation, which poses challenges for the reliable and coordinated operation of the distribution network.
criteria.R: We examine whether electric vehicle (EV) users differ from internal combustion engine vehicle (ICEV) users in real-world driving behavior, and whether observed patterns arise from trip frequency, trip length, or car and user characteristics.
criteria.S: Dual-Active-Bridge (DAB) DC-DC converters are widely used in modern power electronics applications due to their bidirectional power flow, high efficiency, and electrical isolation.
criteria.T: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in electric power and energy systems for forecasting, fault diagnosis, stability assessment, control, renewable energy integration, and real-time monitoring.
criteria.U: Integrating Platinum Group Metal-free (PGM-free) catalysts into High-Temperature Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (HT-PEMFCs) is hindered by phosphoric acid flooding and poor durability.
criteria.V: Distribution network reconfiguration requires switch-state decisions subject to topological and electrical constraints. This paper presents a graph-based surrogate with rooted-forest repair for a modified IEEE 69-bus, two-substation system.
criteria.W: To meet the 6G semantic transmission requirements, this paper proposes an air-ground dual-mode semantic transmission architecture for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface (RIS)-aided Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) networks.
criteria.X: The paper proposes a two-stage optimization model to simultaneous optimal planning and coordinated operation of wind turbines (WTs) and battery energy storage systems (BESS) in a distribution networks.
criteria.Y: Environmental conditions in Laboratory Animal Resource Centers (LARCs), including ammonia, air quality, temperature, humidity, light intensity, and sound level, directly affect animal welfare and experimental reproducibility.
criteria.Z: Conventional Under-Frequency Load Shedding (UFLS) schemes may lead to over-/under-shedding, and they are not quite reliable for application in low-inertia renewable-intensive grids.
criteria.AA: Passenger and freight vehicles generate approximately one quarter of total global greenhouse gas emissions. Mitigating this enormous burden on the transport sector necessitates transition from fossil fuel automobiles to ecological friendly vehicles.
criteria.AB: We investigate isotope effects in hydrogen-related defects in silicon using temperature-dependent capacitance-voltage (C-V) profiling and high-resolution Laplace deep-level transient spectroscopy (Laplace DLTS).
criteria.AC: Transparent ceramic laser materials have been extensively studied for high-power laser applications, where scattering loss is a significant factor affecting laser output power.
criteria.AD: In multi-gateway LoRaWAN deployments, a single uplink packet may be received through several sensor–gateway links, creating link-graph redundancy. We formulate compression as minimum-cardinality selection under aggregate and per-sensor observed-packet coverage constraints.
criteria.AE: A small amount of a synergistically designed and selenophene‐substituted second polymer acceptor, PYISe‐BO‐OD, was incorporated into the PYIT‐OD acceptor layer for enhancing interfacial interactions with the PM6 donor layer, resulting in high‐performance and superior thermal stability in all‐polymer p‐i‐n organic photovoltaics.

questions.instructions:

questions.instructions:
A journal article is titled "Socio-demographic and Cultural Factors Associated with Decision of Married Women on Use Contraceptive Methods in the DRC".

Only one of the following abstract openings comes from that article; the others come from other recent articles in Public Health, Environmental and Occupational Health. Which one is it?

criteria.A: Digital technologies are increasingly being introduced into palliative care. However, little is known about the implementation of new technologies from the perspectives of healthcare professionals and informal caregivers.
criteria.B: Mitochondrial replacement therapy (MRT) encompasses assisted reproductive technologies designed to prevent the transmission of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) mutations by combining the DNA in the nucleus (nuclear genome) of the intending parents with another woman’s enucleated egg that provides healthy donor-derived mtDNA.
criteria.C: Accurate prognostic assessment is essential in palliative care to support treatment planning, goal setting, and communication with patients and families.

criteria.I: The previously published Optimal Resources for Children's Surgical Care (OReCS) addressed disparities in access to high-quality children's surgery in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) with an emphasis on physical and human resources.
criteria.J: Variations in diet quality across the lifespan remain insufficiently characterised, particularly in non-Western populations. We aimed to examine age-and sex-specific variation in diet quality and identify associated dietary components and socio-demographic and lifestyle factors in a Japanese population.

criteria.O: Anopheles funestus s.s plays a major role in sustaining residual malaria transmission in many African settings. criteria.P: This study aimed to assess the quality of life (QOL) among palliative care professionals in the Tabuk region of Saudi Arabia and to identify the factors associated with it.
criteria.Q: We report a rare case of unilateral neuroretinitis associated with dengue infection in a 33-year-old man presenting with acute visual loss in the right eye following a febrile illness acquired during travel to Thailand.

criteria.W: Hypoxanthine guanine xanthine phosphoribosyl transferase (HGXPRT) is one of the central enzymes of purine salvage pathway of protozoan parasites, including Plasmodium.
criteria.X: Obesity has emerged as a significant public health issue in Saudi Arabia, showing regional variations in its prevalence and associated risk factors.

criteria.Z: Preclinical studies suggest that ultraprocessed foods (UPFs) are associated with increased dopaminergic signaling in the striatum, reinforcing intake.
criteria.AA: Digital technologies are becoming increasingly embedded in undergraduate dental curricula, with the potential to support learning and skills development.
criteria.AB: Consumer responses to sustainability-relevant food innovations are associated with psychological factors such as food neophobia (FN), food technology neophobia (FTN), trust, perceived risks and benefits, and food-safety-related perceptions.

questions.instructions:

Title: Secure Consensus in Distributed Systems: Raft Protocol with Hybrid Cryptography

All options are opening lines of abstracts from the field of Computer Networks and Communications. Which option opens the abstract of the work with the title above?

criteria.A: Distributed sensing systems must ultimately reach a single shared decision, whether an alarm, a classification, or a control action. Achieving this is challenging because the two underlying technologies rely on conflicting assumptions.
criteria.B: The expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) has intensified cyber risk in Edge deployments with limited computational resources, where conventional intrusion detection systems are unfeasible.
criteria.C: Class imbalance in network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) creates a trade-off between intrusion sensitivity and false-alarm control. While hybrid resampling methods often improve minority class representation, their effectiveness varies depending on imbalance severity and operational needs.
criteria.D: In the context of intelligent Internet-of-Things (IoT) systems, security can be viewed as preserving symmetry among trusted entities, accurate physical observations, and secure digital interactions despite adversarial threats.
criteria.E: This study presents a synergetic control approach for coordinating the motion of a UAV swarm based on self-organization principles and energy potential interactions.
criteria.F: Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) are particularly challenging for enterprise intrusion detection because they are time-evolving, distributed, and difficult to detect under changing network conditions.
criteria.G: Cyber-physical systems, Industrial IoT, and Industry 4.0 infrastructures are converging rapidly, due to which the attack surface of industrial environments has grown substantially.
criteria.H: Secure data transmission in the Internet of Things (IoT) is a necessity, and the current secure routing paradigms, including trust-based distributed protocols and traditional RPL-based extensions, are usually characterized by high control overhead and high latency in dynamic environments because they cannot adapt to the frequent topology changes.
criteria.I: Machine-learning classifiers deployed in security operations rarely receive timely ground-truth labels, so their health is monitored on an operational dashboard built from label-free proxies: confidence-based accuracy estimators, cross-model agreement, and conformal abstention.
criteria.J: This paper investigates the fixed-time secure consensus problem for disturbed multi-agent systems (MASs) subject to false data injection attacks (FDIAs) via intermittent dynamic event/self-triggered control.
criteria.K: Network threat detection in the Internet of Things must exploit typed relations between devices: a device with unremarkable flow statistics may still be compromised relative to its ownership, co-location, and social ties.
criteria.L: Cloud Computing has emerged as an essential platform for the modern applications. But the growing complexity of the attacks puts pressure on the security of cloud environments.
criteria.M: Power data networks operating over IPv6-enabled communication infrastructures carry heterogeneous grid services with different latency, bandwidth, operational-risk, and recovery-priority requirements.
criteria.N: Secure key generation from shared biometric signals has emerged as a lightweight alternative to traditional cryptographic key distribution, particularly for resource-constrained wearable devices.
criteria.O: The rapid evolution of 5G-NR and the increasing demand for secure and low-latency communications require strong error-correction techniques that are compatible with cryptographic systems.
criteria.P: The rapid proliferation of the Internet of Things (IoT) has positioned the Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) protocol as an important communication standard for large-scale and resource-constrained systems.
criteria.Q: Internet Exchange Points (IXPs) constitute critical infrastructure for reducing dependence on external transit and improving network performance; however, their deployment in rural areas of Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) remains limited, and the adoption of routing security mechanisms is incomplete.
criteria.R: Large-scale distributed systems continuously generate massive volumes of semi-structured and unstructured log data, making manual anomaly detection increasingly impractical.
criteria.S: This article examines how young South Africans use WhatsApp as a back‑channel for co‑viewing Amapiano music videos and live premieres, and how these practices shape participation, visibility, and informal learning in a mobile‑first media ecology.
criteria.T: The rapid advancement of computational systems and digital technologies has significantly transformed modern information infrastructures, industrial operations, and intelligent applications.
criteria.U: The transformation of traditional power grid systems towards smart grids is driven by factors such as the expansion of vehicle charging infrastructure, rapid technological advancements, demands for energy efficiency, as well as the surge in distributed energy generation.
criteria.V: Distributed Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) longevity is heavily constrained by finite battery reserves and data transmission overhead. Balancing energy conservation with link reliability under dynamic node mobility remains a challenge.
criteria.W: The Zinc modelling language was developed as part of the G12 project, which aimed to generate a new approach to constraint programming. A key feature of Zinc was its solver-independence, deliberately designed to separate the modelling of a discrete optimisation problem from how it is solved.
criteria.X: Consensus protocols for computer networks, such as Raft and Paxos, are typically deployed in cloud computing environments and assume that participating nodes possess fixed, known identities for performing log replication.
criteria.Y: A memory exhaustion attack in the Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6) Routing for Low Power and Lossy Networks (RPL) where attacking node inject fake Destination Advertisement Object (DAO) messages to saturate routing tables and isolate legitimate nodes is known by the name Routing Table Overload Attack (RTOA).
criteria.Z: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) devices operating in swarm-like formations—from autonomous device fleets to federated service networks—demands a computing continuum that spans edge nodes, fog gateways, and cloud back-ends.
criteria.AA: With the popularization of Internet of Things (IoT) systems, the risk to denial-of-service (DoS), distributed denial-of-service (DDoS), and wire-tapping jamming attacks has increased, especially in environments where heterogeneous deployment is required and in situations where the adversary is adaptively behaving.
criteria.AB: This paper investigates safe leader-following consensus of heterogeneous nonlinear Caputo fractional-order multi-agent systems under simultaneous denial-of-service (DoS), sensor-deception, and actuator-deception attacks.
criteria.AC: Flat reaction fronts propagating vertically separate fluids with differing densities, which can give rise to hydrodynamic instabilities. This change in density may result from an exothermic reaction or from changes in the chemical composition between reacted and unreacted fluids.
criteria.AD: Future Industrial Internet systems are moving beyond site-bounded automation toward wide-area, distributed, and sustainability-constrained industrial intelligence.
criteria.AE: This study is concerned with the application of consensus control to a class of discrete‐time nonlinear multi‐agent systems with unknown inputs and additive noise.
criteria.AF: Consensus-based distributed task allocation in UAV swarms resolves conflicts through repeated neighbor communication, saturating the ad hoc channel with packet loss and latency; reducing transmission frequency without sacrificing allocation quality is the key challenge.

questions.instructions:

criteria.A: In gas-shielded arc welding, selecting the appropriate gas mixture is crucial not only for welding quality but also for reducing harmful UV radiation, which poses an occupational health risk.
criteria.B: Firefighters in China are routinely exposed to physically and emotionally demanding situations, yet long-running tracking data on their mental-health profile are still scarce.
criteria.C: Burnout among nurses in South Korean public hospitals is an important workforce issue in settings characterized by high job demands and resource constraints.
criteria.D: Approximately 50% of firefighter injuries occur in the musculoskeletal system and poor movement quality increases injury risk.
criteria.E: Pediatric hospitalization is potentially stressful, especially when associated with rare diseases and prolonged treatments, such as Fanconi anemia (FA) and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, which may impact children’s neuropsychomotor and emotional development by restricting daily activities and reducing their occupational repertoire.

criteria.H: Work is defined as “labour or exertion related to the development, production, delivery, or management of objects or services; benefits may be financial or nonfinancial”.

criteria.S: Work stress in nursing education arises when job demands exceedcoping resources, leading to adverse physical, psychological, and social outcomesthat affect performance, well-being, and organizational effectiveness.
criteria.T: Respiratory protection is a critical exposure control strategy in workplaces where airborne hazards are present.
criteria.U: This study aimed to explore the key factors to consider when developing and sharing open-source assistive technology (AAT). To this end, the sip-and-puff mouse was selected from development requests submitted to the Korean Assistive Technology Open Platform.
criteria.V: Wheelchair-mounted robotic arms may support functional autonomy for individuals with upper-limb disabilities, but their long-term usability remains limited by the difficulty of matching high-dimensional robotic control to heterogeneous motor capabilities, daily routines, and task contexts.
criteria.W: Nurses working in high-mortality clinical settings are frequently exposed to patient suffering and death. This might contribute to occupational stress and adverse psychological outcomes.
criteria.X: The Canadian Occupational Performance Measure (COPM) has achieved global implementation across 35 countries in more than 20 language versions. However, its psychometric properties for children with physical disabilities remain unverified.
criteria.Y: Few datasets simultaneously capture occupational exposures and health outcomes in a general working population. To understand associations between occupational exposures and health, researchers often combine existing datasets.
criteria.Z: Hip fractures are a major cause of morbidity and mortality among older adults and frequently require hospitalization and surgical intervention. Patients with hip fractures are particularly vulnerable to pressure ulcers due to immobility, frailty, and comorbidities.
criteria.AA: Identify occupational therapist (OTs) perceived barriers to occupational therapy (OT) access for rural stroke survivors as well as barriers in stroke specific training of therapists.
criteria.AB: Tapioca starch production generates substantial combustible dust exposures governed by IEC 60079-10-2 zone classification.
criteria.AC: Migrant agricultural workers (MAWs), predominantly individuals from countries in the Global South, play a vital role in maintaining Canadian food security.
criteria.AD: This systematic mapping review examines how assistive technology and universal design for learning (UDL) address barriers to participation in inclusive kindergarten-to-grade-12 (K-12) science and science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education.
criteria.AE: Exposure to filler powder particles was evaluated during the manufacturing of 12 biobased nano-enabled polyurethane (PU) foam panels in a research and development facility based on a novel pilot plant technology.
criteria.AF: This study assessed Occupational Health Nursing (OHN) services as a basis for developing wellness programs that promote a healthier work environment in selected hospitals in Manila.

questions.instructions:
Title of a research article: Development and Investigation of a Navigation Electronic Seal System with an Integrated Satellite Communication Channel

criteria.A: The 3GPP channel model TR 38.901 (Release 19) describes the radar cross-section (RCS) of a vehicle as the product of a mean, an angle-dependent pattern and a log-normal random factor, whereas many studies of integrated sensing and communication still use a constant RCS or the Swerling I model.

criteria.H: Vessels disabling their Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponder evade AIS-based analytics.
criteria.I: Earth's radiation budget (ERB) is an essential climate variable, and its continuous observation from space is critical to understanding long-term climate change.
criteria.J: The 3GPP 5G Non-Terrestrial Network (NTN) technology fundamentally relies on a Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) fix at the User Equipment (UE) to pre-compensate for user-link delay and Doppler shifts prior to any transmission, including the random-access procedure for the initial access.
criteria.K: Land subsidence is a geohazard in groundwater-dependent regions, requiring assessment to support hazard mitigation and regional planning. Below are 32 candidates, each the start of a published abstract from the same research area. Which candidate starts the abstract of this study?

criteria.A: Blown powder laser directed energy deposition (DED-LP) is an emerging additive manufacturing process with applications in both new part manufacture and repair of high-value components.
criteria.B: Fruit-specific estimates of failure-related force could support grip force planning in tomato harvesting robots. This study evaluated whether the apparent compression stiffness obtained during pre-bioyield low-load compression can predict the individual mechanical bioyield force.

questions.instructions:
Article title: Understanding the Potential of Nature-based Solutions to Sustainable Livelihood Adaptation: Evidence from Coastal Bangladesh

Which of these abstract beginnings belongs to the article with this title? The other options are taken from different articles in the same subfield.

criteria.A: Diatoms frequently dominate seasonal phytoplankton blooms and contribute ~40% of marine primary production. Viruses drive phytoplankton mortality and bloom collapse, yet how viruses regulate diatom bloom dynamics is not well resolved.
criteria.B: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) serve pivotal roles in elemental geochemical processes, particularly in fluctuating oxic–anoxic environments. Dissolved organic matter (DOM) is a critical component in mediating soil carbon turnover.
criteria.C: The cropland ecosystem is closely linked to global food security and carbon budget dynamics. Understanding the trends and drivers of cropland gross primary productivity (GPP) is essential for evaluating potential agricultural yields and for formulating effective adaptation and even mitigation strategies.
criteria.D: Sustainable livelihood adaptation against climate change-induced shocks requires adequate understanding of integrated impacts on livelihood systems and potential adaptive techniques.
criteria.E: Greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions associated with livestock, crop production and land-use change are important considerations for climate action in Nigeria.
criteria.F: Accurate, spatially resolved agricultural land-use data are essential for estimating water demand, evaluating agricultural production, and understanding long-term changes in managed landscapes.
criteria.G: Accurate estimation of winter wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) aboveground biomass (AGB) is important for crop growth monitoring and field management.
criteria.H: Environmental DNA (eDNA) metabarcoding can provide fish-community inventories across river networks. We surveyed ten sites in the Jingdezhen section of the Raohe River system on 20–23 October 2023 and 2–5 June 2024, covering the Donghe River, Chang River, and Le’an River.
criteria.I: Marine predators frequently form ephemeral multi-predator feeding aggregations around dense prey patches, yet the mechanisms and outcomes of these dynamic events remain poorly resolved.
criteria.J: The critically endangered Chinese bahaba (Bahaba taipingensis) is difficult to monitor via conventional methods due to its low abundance and estuarine habitat.
criteria.K: Mountain forest greenness varies across seasons, yet growing-season averages can mask season-specific relationships with climate variability.
criteria.L: Diverse climatic regions exhibit unique agro-climatic vulnerabilities that are significantly shaped by climate stress. Understanding these distinct vulnerabilities is essential for developing effective policies to mitigate climate change impacts and ensuring sustainable environmental management.
criteria.M: Seasonal lake wetlands perform multiple ecological functions, including flood regulation, maintenance of land-water ecotonal habitats, and support for migratory waterbirds, and therefore play a critical role in regional biodiversity conservation.
criteria.N: Natural coastal ecosystems hold substantial capacity for blue carbon storage, but habitat replacement with harbour and shoreline infrastructure has severely diminished their potential to mitigate climate change.
criteria.O: Ecological corridors that are high in biodiversity potential and stable under climate change are central to long-term conservation planning. Yet spatial prioritization frameworks rarely integrate land-use resistance and climate stability into a unified approach, limiting their operational value for landscape management and policy.
criteria.P: Effective conservation of marine biodiversity requires a strong understanding of how marine systems change over time. Connections between coastal benthic and pelagic systems mean that additional insight may be gained from surveying both habitats alongside each other to investigate if interannual trends are similar.
criteria.Q: In 2016, marsh spits along Fowl River - an oligohaline estuary in coastal Alabama, USA - were identified by community members as a top restoration priority for the Mobile Bay National Estuary Program (MBNEP).
criteria.R: Natural predation where rarity meets rarity raises an important conservation paradox: when one threatened species feeds on another and conservation decisions can be challenging.
criteria.S: Although satellite remote sensing has been widely used to monitor land surface phenology, long-term, high-quality ground-based observations are essential for validating and calibrating these products, particularly for understanding agricultural ecosystem responses to climate change.
criteria.T: The current trends in urbanisation vary across cities and geographic regions (Seto et al. 2013, Zhang 2016) and are creating distinct ecological consequences for urban wild- life (i.e. animals living freely in cities alongside humans) worldwide.
criteria.U: The loose equilibrium (LE) hypothesis predicts that biotic assemblages will exhibit modest change from year-to-year but will not follow directed trajectories away from a stable baseline over longer periods of time.
criteria.V: Coral reefs in the Caribbean Sea continue to experience unprecedented declines driven by the combined impacts of emerging infectious diseases and increasingly frequent marine heatwaves.
criteria.W: Avian schistosomes (AS) are trematodes of significant medical importance as the causative agents of cercarial dermatitis, a re-emerging waterborne human disease.
criteria.X: How retrieval performance varies with simulation settings, neural architecture, and measured-data adaptation remains unclear for hyperspectral crop trait retrieval.
criteria.Y: Understanding how wildlife species differ in their use of time and space in human-influenced, high-altitude landscapes is important for interpreting multispecies associations and informing conservation.
criteria.Z: Environmental variability shapes coral performance, yet its role in structuring host physiology and microbiome composition across reef habitats remains unresolved.
criteria.AA: Implementing the EU Nature Restoration Regulation (EU NRR) requires Member States to monitor multiple indicators of forest biodiversity, yet the role of remote sensing (RS) in this process remains unclear.
criteria.AB: Coastal sediment bacteria mediate essential biogeochemical cycles, yet their functional gene potential to anthropogenic stress gradients remains insufficiently understood.
criteria.AC: Comparing the health impacts of sustainable dietary patterns is challenging due to varying definitions and assessment methods across studies. We aimed to identify, summarise, and discuss these definitions and identify their associated quantitative health impacts.
criteria.AD: Coastal wetlands can serve different ecological functions across the non-breeding season, so a fixed midwinter survey period may not fully represent seasonal bird use.
criteria.AE: Large river deltas are important coastal carbon sinks, yet how changes in sediment supply are associated with subsurface microbial communities and biogeochemical processes remains poorly understood.
criteria.AF: Understanding how habitat structure and spatial configuration jointly influence species abundance is critical for conserving grassland birds in fragmented landscapes.

questions.instructions:
Here is the title of a recently published study: Deep Learning-Based Identification and Tracking of Mesoscale Convective Systems Using Merged Precipitation Products

Below are 32 candidates, each the start of a published abstract from the same research area. Which candidate starts the abstract of this study?

criteria.A: Changes in ice sheet mass manifest as changes in ice flow, ice thickness, and gravitational attraction. These parameters can be measured from space and used to track Greenland's contribution to sea level rise independently from each other.
criteria.B: To improve the accuracy of subglacial reflectivity estimation using ice-sounding radar, this study proposes a method that explicitly incorporates volumetric scattering loss caused by englacial dielectric inhomogeneities.
criteria.C: Daily precipitation estimates over the Haihe River Basin show strong terrain-related error contrasts. We developed a regional two-stage post-processing fusion workflow for five gridded precipitation products.
criteria.D: The impact of mesoscale vertical motion on the thermodynamic, microphysical, and convective transformations of marine cold air outbreaks (MCAOs) is still largely unknown, partly due to scarce high-resolution observations in upstream Arctic regions.
criteria.E: Better understanding how convective processes impact the isotopic composition of atmospheric water has implications for understanding present-day phenomena such as squall lines or tropical cyclones, and for reconstructions of past rainfall extreme events.
criteria.F: Stable carbon isotopes (δ13C) of benthic foraminifera are widely used to reconstruct past changes in deep water circulation, carbon storage, and ventilation.
criteria.G: This study investigated the impact of an extreme precipitation event and the subsequent landslides that occurred in São Sebastião municipality (São Paulo State, Brazil) in February 2023 on particulate matter (PM 10 and PM 2.5 ) concentration.
criteria.H: Accurate representation of flow‐dependent background‐error covariance is essential for modern ensemble–variational data assimilation systems, but estimating ensemble covariance from sufficiently large ensembles remains computationally expensive.
criteria.I: While recent advancements in tropical cyclone prediction have been extensively documented, existing review literature remains heavily fragmented into isolated academic domains, such as artificial intelligence, data assimilation, or coastal hydrodynamics.
criteria.J: Treeline ecotones are key indicators of environmental change, yet their responses to climate warming vary markedly across landscapes. This study investigates how elevation and local environmental contexts moderate warming effects on treeline dynamics.
criteria.K: The effect of urban land use on convective storms with deep and persistent rotating updrafts (supercell storms) is systematically investigated using ensembles of idealized numerical simulations.
criteria.L: Areal Reduction Factors (ARFs) are widely used to convert point design precipitation derived from intensity–duration–frequency (IDF) curves into areal precipitation values for hydrological design.
criteria.M: Accurate snow depth (SD) estimation in forested mountain environments remains challenging owing to terrain complexity and vegetation effects.
criteria.N: Rapid glacier retreat in the Western Himalaya caused by climate change has substantially transformed glacier and glacial-lake systems, increasing the likelihood of glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs).
criteria.O: Mesoscale convective systems (MCSs) are organized convective precipitation regions that produce severe weather hazards, including heavy rainfall, flooding, and strong winds.
criteria.P: To better represent real-world traffic emissions there is growing emphasis on measuring UFPs nearby traffic hotspots. Currently, the UFPs are monitored in Europe as PNSD measurements in the size range 10–800 nm using an MPSS.
criteria.Q: Lake-effect snow (LES) has traditionally been studied from a mesoscale perspective, with comparatively less attention devoted to the role of synoptic-scale forcing.
criteria.R: Storm surge is a major coastal hazard in the East China Sea. A coupled tide–surge model forced by blended parametric typhoon and reanalysis winds was used to examine sensitivity to typhoon track, central pressure, radius of maximum wind (Rmax), and translation speed, with Typhoon Winnie (1997) as the baseline.
criteria.S: Sediment color is a valuable proxy in paleoceanography, reflecting chemical and mineralogical composition influenced by biogeochemical processes and depositional environments.
criteria.T: Glaciovolcanic products are important proxies for paleoenvironmental reconstructions in volcanic regions, especially when these products can be dated.
criteria.U: Accurate quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) is critical for responding to severe weather events such as heavy rainfall. Deep learning (DL) methods, which can establish nonlinear mappings between radar observations and rain rate (R), have been widely applied to reduce QPE errors.
criteria.V: Wind turbine clutter (WTC) can severely degrade the quality of meteorological radar data, particularly under complex weather conditions. Because WTC echoes can substantially overlap with precipitation echoes, they may introduce considerable errors into weather identification and forecasting.
criteria.W: Atmospheric new particle formation is driven by condensable vapors such as sulfuric acid and highly oxygenated organic molecules (HOMs). Measuring these gases is challenging because they are present at trace concentrations, they are easily lost through condensation onto surfaces, and they include a wide range of chemically diverse species.
criteria.X: Snow and glacier meltwater are critical water resources for mountain regions, yet their accurate representation in hydrological models remains challenging.
criteria.Y: Accurate radar-based quantitative precipitation estimation (QPE) plays a critical role in disaster prevention and reduction. In mountainous terrain, blockage of low-elevation radar beams can lead to missing low-level precipitation observations, while errors in specific differential phase KDP retrieval further limit QPE accuracy.
criteria.Z: Quasi‐stationary band‐shaped precipitation systems (QBPSs) are the major cause of localized heavy‐rainfall events (HREs) in Japan. criteria.AA: The impact of long-term snow cover variability on winter tourism in the mountainous areas of Poland is an increasingly important research topic, particularly in light of the anticipated effects of climate change.
criteria.AB: Fast and accurate calculation of atmospheric transmittance is essential for infrared atmospheric remote sensing and satellite data assimilation. However, fast radiative transfer models show significant errors in strong water vapour absorption channels (e.g., near 6.7 μm).
criteria.AC: A model for the gas nucleation pressure below the vapour pressure is crucial for predicting cavitation in nozzles and valves and for flashing inception in pipelines.
criteria.AD: Glacier–proglacial lake interactions can accelerate terminus retreat and dynamic thinning of lake-terminating glaciers. However, glacier responses to abrupt lake disconnection following glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) remain poorly quantified.
criteria.AE: We develop a random analog predictor (RAP) algorithm for the forecasting of Arctic sea ice extent (SIE) on seasonal timescales. This is a stochastic variant for scalar time series of the method of the analogues that only uses the historical SIE record to produce ensemble forecasts.
criteria.AF: North Africa and the Middle East are profoundly impacted by intense dust storms driven by Saharan cyclones, which generate the sustained surface winds necessary for regional aerosol uplift and transport.

questions.instructions:

criteria.W: We present a novel subspace segment tree data structure designed for online aggregation queries on streaming data, addressing the challenge of efficient query processing under limited storage space in embedded systems.

criteria.Z: Dynamic task allocation in multi-unmanned-aerial-vehicle (multi-UAV) teams must account for uncertain task return, changing reachability, intermittent communication, and terminal-return energy.

questions.instructions:

criteria.Y: Antibiotic-associated gastrointestinal dysbiosis can compromise microbial homeostasis and mucosal health, creating a need for natural feed additives that support gastrointestinal resilience.

criteria.AB: Oilseed processing can alter lipid accessibility during digestion, potentially affecting microbial activity, nutrient utilization, and animal performance in high-concentrate feeding systems.
criteria.AC: Methionine plays a central role in methyl metabolism and glutathione synthesis, and its availability can influence the partitioning of methyl groups toward lipid metabolism and antioxidant defenses.
criteria.AD: Phenological responses of camelina to management were evaluated using days after planting (DAP) and cumulative growing degree days (GDD) at nine main BBCH stages.
criteria.AE: Precise coordination between ovulation and insemination is essential for optimizing fixed-time artificial insemination (FTAI) in sows.

All options are opening lines of abstracts from the field of Cardiology and Cardiovascular Medicine. Which option opens the abstract of the work with the title above?

criteria.J: Intracellular calcium waves in cardiac myocytes propagate through a fire-diffuse-fire mechanism in which calcium released from one RyR2 cluster diffuses to neighboring clusters and triggers their activation.

criteria.Z: Maladaptive ventricular remodeling is the major pathological process linking myocardial infarction (MI) to heart failure, yet its upstream molecular drivers remain incompletely defined.
criteria.AA: Acute heart failure (AHF) is prone to early clinical deterioration. The prognostic nutritional index (PNI), derived from serum albumin and lymphocyte count, is readily available.
criteria.AB: Fabry disease is an X-linked lysosomal storage disorder that can cause progressive cardiomyopathy, myocardial fibrosis, conduction disease, and malignant ventricular arrhythmias.

questions.instructions:

criteria.X: Generative artificial intelligence (GAI) hallucinations raise questions about how users respond to unreliable outputs from a technology on which they depend.
criteria.Y: LGBTQ+ youth in Eswatini navigate identity and well-being within social environments shaped by cultural expectations, legal restrictions, family relationships, educational institutions, and community attitudes.
criteria.Z: Emotional resilience is a key psychological resource for maintaining well-being and adaptation in the workplace and is closely associated with perceived emotional intelligence.
criteria.AA: Medical students face prolonged training, rigorous assessment, and professional demands that may affect their subjective well-being.
criteria.AB: This analysis unpacks how interstate conflicts change the scope and function of memory laws. Following diplomatic ruptures, memory entrepreneurs deploy conflict-time memory laws to essentialize adversaries, cause them reputational damage, and communicate specific interpretations of the conflict to both domestic and international audiences.
criteria.AC: The rapid transformation of labour markets, accelerated digitalisation, artificial intelligence, automation and changing business models are fundamentally reshaping the requirements imposed on human capital in joint-stock companies.
criteria.AD: Teachers’ professional self-efficacy is one of the key determinants of the quality of early childhood education; however, there is little empirical evidence available on the personal psychological resources underlying its development within the Hungarian preschool education context.
criteria.AE: The present research is the inaugural application of the conceptual framework of attachment theory to investigate the correlation between adult attachment styles in professional settings and employee communication methods.
criteria.AF: Youth wellbeing has become a keyword in contemporary media discourses, public policy, and academic scholarship in response to the growing prevalence of mental health difficulties among young people.

questions.instructions:
Find the abstract that matches a title.

Title: Ancestral Mother–Infant Interaction and Its Relevance for the Evolution of Arts

All options are opening lines of abstracts from the field of Cultural Studies. Which option opens the abstract of the work with the title above?

criteria.A: Many ancient and historic Mediterranean cities have undergone periods of rapid urban expansion during the past few centuries, often involving the replacement of agricultural landscapes that once surrounded them with industrial, commercial and residential landcover.
criteria.B: This article considers the relationship between melancholia, temporality, and maternity in Jennifer Kent’s The Babadook (2014), using the film as a case study to theorise the relationship between melancholia and cinematic form.
criteria.C: This study aims to uncover and explain the concept and model of flexibility as a mechanism for the sustainability of folk performing arts amidst conditions of social and cultural change.
criteria.D: This study examines the Perang Ketupat tradition in Tempilang Village, Bangka Belitung Province, Indonesia, as a form of cultural performance. It aims to analyze the tradition through five dimensions: ritual, performing arts, community participation, cultural education, and community-based safeguarding of intangible cultural heritage (ICH).
criteria.E: This article examines Freud’s treatment of panic in Group Psychology and the Analysis of the Ego , where it appears as both the affect of group disintegration and an ill-defined form of anxiety.
criteria.F: This study examines the relevance of the concept of kafa’ah in Islamic law and Mandar customs through a case study in Polewali Mandar Regency. The purpose of this study is to determine the concept of kafa’ah in Mandar customs according to traditional leaders and cultural experts, the Islamic legal perspective on kafa’ah, and the relevance of both.
criteria.G: Interfaith interaction between Buddhist and Hindu communities in Banyuasin Regency remains underexplored, particularly regarding Buddhist participation in Hindu religious rituals.
criteria.H: This position paper examines how the gap between higher music education and contemporary labour reshapes cultural management in classical music. We argue that youth orchestras, Young Artist Programmes and opera studios function as liminal institutions between education and employment, artistic development and employability, care and competition.
criteria.I: Religious traditions in Indonesian Muslim communities are the result of the dynamic interaction between Islamic teachings and local culture. One example is the Takbir Festival in North Anjatan Village, which serves not only as a religious ritual but also as a social and cultural platform involving broad community participation.
criteria.J: Neduta/Nebolai is a premarital proposal ritual among the Kaili people that involves families, customary elders, religious figures, and culturally meaningful symbols.
criteria.K: This study examines how two leading news organisations operating in contrasting political and media systems, the BBC in the United Kingdom and Al Arabiya in Saudi Arabia, framed COVID-19 in content distributed through their official X (formerly Twitter) accounts between January 2020 and February 2022.
criteria.L: The process of digitalization has transformed not only the gaming industry but also the television series sector. While television series were once confined to broadcast media, they are now accessible anytime and anywhere through internet-based digital platforms, transcending traditional temporal and spatial limitations.
criteria.M: Especially in transcultural fandoms, misunderstandings around interpretive norms and conventions can spark conflict. This article looks at misunderstandings between fan genres that deal with male/male relationships—English-language slash fandom, Chinese danmei fandom, and Chinese dangai (danmei adaptations).
criteria.N: This essay argues that Indigenous relational ontologies provide a foundational framework for rethinking art historical method in ecological terms.
criteria.O: Sandur is a traditional art form that continues to be preserved in Klampis District, Bangkalan Regency. Besides serving as entertainment and a means of cultural preservation, Sandur provides economic benefits through the involvement of artists and economic activities surrounding performances.
criteria.P: Drawing on ethnographic data, this perspective examines the symbiotic relationship between play and household chores in the everyday lives of young Indigenous Yucatec Maya children.
criteria.Q: This study examines whether material culture can serve as a proxy for past social interaction. Using the ArchMatNet agent-based model, we simulate social behavior in small-scale communities and resulting material culture production, then compare social and material culture networks.
criteria.R: Social learning and innovation are fundamental processes in cultural evolution, yet their interaction remains poorly understood. Prior research suggests that inheriting social information reduces exploration.
criteria.S: This article traces Laura Meneses’s anticolonial activism in defense of Puerto Rico’s independence through her shifting citizenship and hemispheric residences.
criteria.T: This community service program supported the hadroh group of the Student Communication Forum – Jambi Kota Seberang (FKM-JKS), a student organization with considerable cultural potential but limited organized development of its Islamic performing arts.
criteria.U: The rapid expansion of digital streaming and the complexity of cross-border audience engagement define the contemporary media landscape.
criteria.V: The Belian Ritual is a traditional healing ritual practiced by the Paser ethnic community in North Penajam Paser Regency, combining spiritual, social, and cultural elements.
criteria.W: This study aims to demonstrate the integration of Al-Qur'an and the Javanese culture of Tepo Seliro and how the implementation in Muslim and non-Muslim relations to realize the people's peace and harmony lives in diversity in Indonesia.
criteria.X: This paper investigates Wolfgang Buttress’s art installation The Hive, which features a musical soundtrack recorded in cooperation with a colony of honeybees.
criteria.Y: Art making, understood as making music, dancing, and producing visual artworks, has a deep evolutionary history. Traces of musical instruments, figurative arts, and rock art, like engravings and cupules, are found all around Europe, Asia, and Africa since the Pleistocene.
criteria.Z: During the last three decades of the nineteenth century, Presbyterian and Methodist Mission Homes in San Francisco were established by women seeking to rescue and Christianize Chinese “slave girls”—girls and young women they understood to have been sold into household labor or prostitution or trapped in other unfree relationships.
criteria.AA: Humans are both individual and social beings who require interaction to meet their needs and achieve personal growth. Amidst the diversity of Indonesian society, interfaith tolerance is a crucial aspect of maintaining unity, supporting development, and reducing social inequality.
criteria.AB: Contemporary practices of tapping into the wisdom of ancestral trees are described through three entangled recent events lived within the context of Bantu practices in Cameroon.
criteria.AC: This study aims to reconstruct the understanding of Islamization in Southeast Asia through a comparative analysis of Indonesia and Malaysia, emphasizing the relationship between origin narratives and the dynamics of Islamic development.
criteria.AD: This study investigates the identity work of critical accountants in the face of ecological crises, drawing on 28 semi-structured interviews and an autoethnographic account.
criteria.AE: The proliferation of smartphones across everyday life has forced us to rethink human subjectivity, and subsequently, who counts as the ‘digital’ or ‘posthuman’ subject.
criteria.AF: This critical and theoretical essay discusses the weakness of the concept of toleration as a normative horizon for addressing cultural and linguistic diversity in Greek lower secondary school and suggests the redefinition of belonging, power and intercultural safety.
